rules.description: Switch between open Mac windows with a visual picker.
rules.documentation:
## Switch between Mac windows with a visual picker

Use this Rule when several applications have multiple windows and cycling through apps is slower than choosing the exact window you need. The shortcut opens Rulr's interactive window switcher, where you select a window to bring it into focus.

Unlike switching between applications, the picker lets you choose a specific window exposed by an app. It is useful when the app you need has several windows open.

To choose between this Rule and a dedicated switching app, compare [Mac window switchers and AltTab alternatives](/posts/mac-window-switchers/). The guide covers window previews, search, and browser-tab navigation so you can choose the features you need before importing.

**When:** Press Option + Tab, or your replacement shortcut. **Do:** Show Window Switcher. There is no If Condition. The sample uses a horizontal layout and an empty application-exclusion list, so it starts without a custom filter for your work apps.

## Configure and try it

1. Import using **Open this Rule in Rulr** and review Hotkey Pressed. Choose an unused combination if Option + Tab belongs to another window tool.
2. Review the switcher layout and excluded applications. Add exclusions if windows from a particular app should stay out of the picker.
3. Grant Accessibility access so Rulr can work with application windows and focus the selection. Keep a few ordinary windows open in different apps for your first trial.
4. Press the shortcut, choose a window, and verify that the intended window becomes active. Repeat with another app and check how exclusions affect the available choices.

Choose the switcher when you want to decide which window becomes active. To move a particular application's window after a monitor change, use [Monitor Workspace](/rules/arrange-windows-monitor-mac/) instead. Review [Show Window Switcher](/capabilities/actions/#action.window.show-window-switcher) for its settings, or read the [Mac automation guide](/posts/mac-automation/) before connecting window Actions to other events.

## Requirements and limits

The sample's Trigger and Action are available without Pro. Accessibility is required for the switcher, not only for recording the hotkey.

The picker works with windows exposed by applications; it is not a browser tab search, document-content search, or saved-session restore tool. Application-specific window behavior can affect which entries are available. For navigating individual Chrome tabs rather than application windows, use [Search Chrome Windows and Tabs](/rules/search-chrome-windows-tabs/).

## Is a window switcher the same as a window manager?

This Rule handles choosing and focusing an open window. It does not tile, resize, or restore window layouts. For positioning a chosen app's window when a monitor connects, use [Monitor Workspace](/rules/arrange-windows-monitor-mac/). Choose the task you need before importing either Rule.

For built-in tiling and dedicated snapping tools, see the [Mac window manager comparison](/posts/window-manager-mac/).
rules.intro:
Switch between open windows on Mac with a visual window picker. Press Option + Tab, choose the window you need, and bring it into focus with Rulr.

The sample opens a horizontal picker with no apps excluded. Choose your shortcut, layout, and app exclusions after importing to keep the list focused on the windows you use.
rules.title: Window Switcher

rules.description: Capture, recognize, and translate text anywhere on your Mac screen.
rules.documentation:
## Translate screenshot and image text visible on screen

This Rule is useful when text is visible but cannot be selected normally, such as a screenshot or an application label. It captures the configured screen target, recognizes the image's text, translates it, and displays a result panel.

**When:** Press the configured hotkey, initially Option + Space. **Do:** Capture Screen or Window, recognize text in the captured image, translate that Text output into English, and show the translated result. There is no If Condition. The sample capture target is a full screen rather than a manually selected phrase.

## Configure and try it

1. Import with **Open this Rule in Rulr** and review the shortcut and screen capture target. Choose a distinct hotkey and an appropriate capture area for your workflow.
2. Review the target language in Translate Text. The sample uses English; select another available language if needed.
3. Grant Screen Recording permission and complete the Translation Shortcut setup requested by Rulr for macOS System Translate. Grant Accessibility if recording a replacement shortcut requires it.
4. Display a short sentence in a clear font, run the Rule, and compare the recognized and translated meaning with the source. Test your usual language and layout before using longer material.

If you need the source text without translation, use [Copy Text from Your Screen](/rules/copy-text-mac-screen/). Compare [Recognize Text in Image](/capabilities/actions/#action.image.recognize-text-in-image) with the capture step to see which output feeds recognition. The [AI Builder guide](/posts/build-mac-automations-with-ai/#3-review-it-on-the-visual-canvas) explains how to review a multi-step Rule before enabling it.

## Requirements and limits

Recognize Text in Image requires Rulr Pro. Screen capture permission and the translation setup are separate requirements; granting one does not complete the other.

OCR mistakes can carry into the translation, especially with small text or mixed columns. The sample displays the result without copying it, inserting it into another app, or replacing text on the screen. For text that can already be selected, see [Translate Selected Text](/rules/translate-selected-text-mac/).

## Screen translation or selected-text translation?

Screen translation is useful when an image or app label has no selectable text: OCR supplies the text before translation. For a passage you can highlight, selected-text translation avoids that recognition step. To keep the original wording without translating it, choose [Copy Text from Your Screen](/rules/copy-text-mac-screen/).

{{< published-post-link path="/posts/ocr-for-mac-images-screenshots" label="Choose an OCR method for images and screenshots on Mac" >}}
rules.intro:
Translate text on your Mac screen with a keyboard shortcut, including text in images or screenshots. Rulr captures it, runs OCR, and shows the translation.

The sample captures the full screen and translates the recognized text into English. Review the capture target, choose your target language, and complete the Translation Shortcut setup after importing.
requiredConfiguration: Choose a shortcut
Choose a target language
rules.title: Translate Screen Text

rules.description: Append selected text to a notes file from any supported app.
rules.documentation:
## Append selected passages to a notes file

This Rule is useful for collecting short passages while reading documentation or reviewing a document. It appends the current selection to a text file, so you can build a local reading queue without moving between the source app and a notes editor.

**When:** Press the configured hotkey, initially Option + Space. **Do:** Get Selected Text, then Write to File using append-to-end mode. There is no If Condition. The sample destination is `~/Downloads/Rulr Notes.txt`; each run supplies the selection as the content to append.

## Configure and try it

1. Import through **Open this Rule in Rulr** and choose a shortcut that does not conflict with another app or Rule.
2. Select the actual destination file in Write to File and keep append-to-end mode if you want to retain earlier entries.
3. Allow Accessibility and System Events Automation access for selection retrieval, and ensure Rulr can write to the destination.
4. Select a short test passage in a compatible app, run the shortcut, and inspect the file. Repeat with a different passage to verify that the previous content remains and the new content is appended.

## Requirements and limits

Write to File requires Rulr Pro. Reading a selection depends on the source application's support, and some apps may briefly use the clipboard as part of retrieval.

The sample saves selected text only. It does not automatically include the source URL, title, timestamp, or separators between entries; add those to the content if your note format needs them. It also does not capture text from an image. For visible text that cannot be selected, use [Copy Text from Your Screen](/rules/copy-text-mac-screen/).
rules.intro:
Save selected text from a Mac app to a notes file with one keyboard shortcut, without switching away from the current document or webpage.

Choose the shortcut and destination text file after importing the Rule. Each run gets the current selection and appends it to the end of that file.
requiredConfiguration: Choose a shortcut
Choose a notes file
rules.title: Save Selected Text

rules.description: Set volume by audio device and open your music app when needed.
rules.documentation:
## Apply volume when the output device changes

This Rule is useful when headphones and speakers need different starting volume levels. It reacts to the audio output device selected by macOS, checks its name, and applies the corresponding branch rather than requiring you to adjust volume manually after every switch.

**When:** The audio output device changes. **If:** Its name contains `AirPods`, set volume to 20 and launch Spotify. In the separate `Speakers` branch, set volume to 30. Devices matching neither name receive no Action from the sample.

## Configure and try it

1. Import with **Open this Rule in Rulr** and review the exact names macOS reports for your audio outputs.
2. Replace the name fragments in the Conditions with values that identify your devices. Choose distinct matches if each device should use only one branch.
3. Set comfortable volume levels and review the Spotify launch Action. Select an installed music app, remove that step, or keep Spotify if it belongs in your routine.
4. Enable the Rule and switch outputs using macOS Sound controls. Check the resulting volume and whether the intended app launches. Try an unmatched device too.

To change the device itself rather than only its volume, compare [Switch Audio Output](/rules/switch-audio-output-mac/). The [Variables library](/capabilities/variables/) lists audio state values, and the [Mac automation guide](/posts/mac-automation/) shows how device events and Conditions fit into a Rule.

## Requirements and limits

The sample's components are available without Pro and declare no special permission. The music app must be installed if you retain its launch Action, and the output device must support the requested volume change.

The Rule responds to an output-device change, not merely a Bluetooth connection. It does not connect headphones, start playback, or maintain a continuous volume limit. For choosing an output with a manual shortcut first, use [Switch Audio Output](/rules/switch-audio-output-mac/).
rules.intro:
Set Mac volume automatically when the audio output device changes, using different levels for AirPods and speakers and opening Spotify when needed.

Additional device-name branches can pair Set Volume and Launch Application Actions with meetings, music, office speakers, or headphones.
rules.title: Set Volume by Audio Device

rules.description: Translate selected text on your Mac and show the result.
rules.documentation:
## Translate text exposed by the frontmost app

Use this Rule as a base for checking a short passage in another language. It reads an application's selected text, translates the retrieved value into English, and presents the result in Rulr rather than altering the original document.

**When:** The exact phrase `;translate` is typed. **Do:** Get Selected Text, translate that Text output, and display the translated text. There is no If Condition. The default target language is English, and the supplied Trigger is typed text rather than a hotkey.

## Configure and try it

1. Import using **Open this Rule in Rulr** and review the Trigger phrase and target language.
2. Grant Accessibility and System Events Automation for retrieving the selection. Complete the Translation Shortcut setup requested by Rulr for macOS System Translate.
3. Test a short selection in a compatible application. Check whether typing `;translate` changes the selection before Get Selected Text can read it.
4. If the phrase replaces or disturbs selected text in your app, change the Trigger to Hotkey Pressed. Select the passage again, invoke the new shortcut, and compare the displayed translation with the intended source.

## Requirements and limits

Text Typed requires Rulr Pro. Selection retrieval depends on the source app exposing text, and some apps may briefly use the clipboard. Translation also needs the configured macOS translation workflow and a supported language.

The Rule displays the result; it does not automatically replace the passage, copy the translation, or translate an entire document. Review important wording yourself, particularly after an empty or unexpected selection. For visible text that cannot be selected, use [Translate Screen Text](/rules/translate-screen-text-mac/).
rules.intro:
Translate selected text on your Mac by typing a short trigger, then display the English translation without leaving the app you are working in.

The final display can give way to Insert Text, Set Clipboard to Text, or Write to File, extending the flow into inline translation, writing, or replies.
rules.title: Translate Selected Text

rules.description: Turn text on screen into copyable text.
rules.documentation:
## How this Rule works

Option-Space starts full-screen recognition and displays the OCR output. Change the shortcut or capture target if needed.

## Configure and try it

Import the Rule, review its Trigger and Actions, and adjust the settings described above before enabling it. Test the result in a safe, temporary context.

## Requirements and limits

Grant Accessibility for the shortcut and Screen Recording access for capture. Recognition depends on visible text; this Rule displays the result rather than copying it automatically.
rules.intro:
Press a shortcut to recognize text on the full Mac screen and show the result in a panel.

Option-Space starts full-screen recognition and displays the OCR output. Change the shortcut or capture target if needed.
rules.title: Recognize Screen Text

rules.description: Clean up entered text and copy it for pasting anywhere.
rules.documentation:
## Remove whitespace around entered text

This Rule gives you a small text-cleaning prompt when a copied value has unwanted whitespace at its edges. You supply the text, Rulr applies Trim, and the cleaned result goes to the clipboard for use in another app.

**When:** The exact phrase `;rulr` is typed. **Do:** Ask for input, transform that input with Trim, and copy the transformed Text Result. There is no If Condition. The prompt is configured to stop the Rule when cancelled, so cancellation should not continue to the clipboard Action.

## Configure and try it

1. Import with **Open this Rule in Rulr** and review Text Typed. Replace the trigger with a distinctive phrase if `;rulr` conflicts with another routine.
2. Check the input prompt and keep Transform Text connected to the prompt's Input Variable. Keep Set Clipboard to Text connected to the transformation result.
3. Grant Accessibility access for the typed Trigger. Enable the Rule and enter the phrase in a temporary document.
4. Supply a value with spaces or line breaks before and after the meaningful text. Paste the result into a temporary note and compare it with the input. Try cancelling the prompt on a second run.

## Requirements and limits

Text Typed and Transform Text require Rulr Pro. The source is the text entered into the prompt; the sample does not automatically read a selection or the previous clipboard content.

Trim removes surrounding whitespace rather than rewriting internal spacing, fixing grammar, or changing letter case. Copying the result replaces the previous clipboard text without pasting it automatically. For encoding a clipboard value and inserting it directly, see [Paste URL-Encoded Text](/rules/url-encode-paste-text-mac/).
rules.intro:
Trim unwanted spaces and line breaks from text on your Mac, then copy the cleaned result to the clipboard so it is ready to paste.

Transform Text can use another transformation, while Insert Text or Write to File can carry the result into pasted copy, notes, messages, or structured text.
rules.title: Trim Text

rules.description: Extract text from new images added to a watched folder.
rules.documentation:
## Automate image OCR for a watched folder

This Rule turns an image inbox into a text review workflow. When a new receipt image, screenshot, or reference picture arrives, it recognizes the image's text and displays the result in Rulr so you can check it without opening a separate OCR tool.

**When:** A direct item is added to Downloads. **If:** Its filename matches a PNG, JPEG, HEIC, or WebP extension. **Do:** Recognize text in the event's Item Path, then show the recognized text in a panel. The display receives the OCR output rather than a fixed sample sentence.

## Configure and try it

1. Import with **Open this Rule in Rulr** and choose the folder where your image files arrive.
2. Review the image-name Condition and keep the OCR source connected to the Trigger's Item Path.
3. Check that Show Text or Image uses the recognized Text output. Enable the Rule and add a clear image containing a short sentence you can compare with the result.
4. Try another image with your usual language and layout. Confirm that a nonmatching document does not enter the image branch.

Use this folder workflow for incoming image files, and [Copy Text from Your Screen](/rules/copy-text-mac-screen/) for content already visible in an app. Check [Recognize Text in Image](/capabilities/actions/#action.image.recognize-text-in-image) for the Action's input and Text output. To adapt the displayed result into a different workflow, follow the [AI Builder review and refinement steps](/posts/build-mac-automations-with-ai/#3-review-it-on-the-visual-canvas) and verify that later Actions consume the OCR result.

## Requirements and limits

Folder monitoring and image OCR require Rulr Pro, plus access to the selected folder. This workflow reads image files; it does not capture the screen or extract every page of a PDF.

Recognition can lose punctuation, line order, or characters in small or blurred text. The watcher is not recursive and does not process the existing folder contents automatically. To capture visible text directly, use [Copy Text from Your Screen](/rules/copy-text-mac-screen/).

## Can I extract text from an existing image or PDF?

To try an existing image, add a disposable copy to the watched folder after enabling the Rule. For an image already open on screen, use the screen OCR Rule instead. The filename filter and OCR input here are for image files; this is not PDF OCR or a batch conversion of existing documents.

{{< published-post-link path="/posts/ocr-for-mac-images-screenshots" label="Compare built-in OCR, screen shortcuts, and image-folder automation" >}}
rules.intro:
Extract text from new images automatically on Mac. Watch a folder for PNG, JPEG, HEIC, and WebP files, then use OCR to display the recognized text.

The sample watches Downloads, checks each arriving filename, and passes the matching file path to image OCR. Choose your image inbox after importing; this Rule displays the result without saving or copying it automatically.
requiredConfiguration: Choose a watched folder
rules.title: Extract Text from New Images

rules.description: Open the right work apps automatically for each work session.
rules.documentation:
## Launch your chosen app set from one shortcut

This Rule brings a group of work applications into a single keyboard routine. It is useful when beginning a writing, design, or team session that consistently needs several apps, while allowing time Conditions to restrict when the shortcut performs the launches.

**When:** Press Option + W. **If:** The current time is before 12:00 or at or after 13:00. **Do:** Launch Slack, Notion, and Figma. The sample uses an OR match, so either time Condition allows the launches. It excludes the noon hour but does not restrict the Rule to weekdays or impose an evening end time.

## Configure and try it

1. Import with **Open this Rule in Rulr** and review the hotkey. Grant Accessibility if you need to record a different shortcut.
2. Select the applications installed on your Mac in each Launch Application Action. Remove apps you do not need or add further launch Actions for your own workspace.
3. Review both time Conditions and their match mode. Choose explicit boundaries and the appropriate AND or OR logic if your intended working hours differ from the sample.
4. Enable the Rule and test at an allowed time. Check that each application launches, then test the excluded interval by temporarily adjusting the Conditions and restoring them afterward.

## Requirements and limits

The sample's Trigger and Actions are available without Pro. Each selected app must be installed and available to the Mac user running Rulr.

Launching an app does not automatically log in, open a particular project, or restore window positions. This is a hotkey routine rather than a schedule. For a weekday launch time, see [Launch Apps at a Scheduled Time](/rules/launch-apps-at-time-mac/).
rules.intro:
Open your work apps with one Mac keyboard shortcut during your chosen work hours, so Slack, Notion, Figma, or another app set is ready together.

Different Launch Application Actions and Conditions can turn the same shortcut into a meeting starter, study setup, design workspace, or another repeatable app-launch routine. To build your own routine through conversation, follow [How to Build Mac Automations with AI](/posts/build-mac-automations-with-ai/).
rules.title: Open Work Apps

rules.description: Route images, PDFs, and archives from Downloads into the right folders.
rules.documentation:
## Sort new downloads into folders by file type

This Rule separates common downloads into image, PDF, and archive destinations. It is useful for an inbox workflow where pictures should go to a visual review folder, documents to a reading queue, and compressed files to an archive folder.

**When:** A direct item is added to the watched Downloads folder. **If:** Its filename matches one of three branches. **Do:** Move that item's path to the corresponding destination. The image branch matches PNG, JPEG, HEIC, and WebP names; the PDF branch checks `.pdf`; the archive branch matches ZIP, 7z, TAR, and GZ names.

## Configure and try it

1. Import with **Open this Rule in Rulr** and select the source folder on your Mac.
2. Review all three Move File or Folder Actions. The sample paths are Pictures/Inbox, Documents/PDF Inbox, and Downloads/Archives; select destinations that exist and suit your workflow.
3. Keep each Action connected to the Trigger's Item Path Variable and review the numbered-name conflict option.
4. Add disposable examples of an image, PDF, and archive. Confirm that each reaches its intended folder. Add an unrelated text file and check that it stays in Downloads.

Compare the other [Mac file automation tasks](/rules/files-organization/) before adding more branches. [Folder Contents Changed](/capabilities/#trigger.input.folder-contents-changed) provides the Item Path used by the move Actions; the [Mac automation guide](/posts/mac-automation/#how-rulr-automates-your-mac) explains how event outputs and Conditions connect.

## Requirements and limits

Folder monitoring and moving files require Rulr Pro. Allow access to each folder involved. The Rule matches names, without inspecting file contents, unpacking archives, or sorting files already in the folder.

The watcher is not recursive, and an added-item event is not a guarantee that a download is complete. Try the browsers and download tools you normally use. For a narrower workflow with one destination, use [Organize Downloaded PDFs](/rules/organize-downloaded-pdfs-mac/).

## Will this clean up old downloads or delete files?

The sample moves new matching items; it does not delete downloads or scan an existing backlog. Files that match none of the three branches stay where they are. For sorting incoming photos and videos into separate folders, use [Import Media](/rules/sort-photos-videos-mac/).

{{< published-post-link path="/posts/hazel-alternative" label="Compare Rulr and Hazel for Mac file automation" >}}
rules.intro:
Automatically organize your Downloads folder on Mac by file type. Move new images, PDFs, and archives into separate folders with an editable Rulr Rule.

Three filename Conditions route each matching arrival to its destination, using numbered names for conflicts. Choose the watched folder and all three destinations before enabling it; existing downloads are not processed automatically.
requiredConfiguration: Choose a watched Downloads folder and destination folders
rules.title: Sort Downloads

rules.description: Capture a thought without leaving the current app.
rules.documentation:
## Capture quick notes in a plain text file on Mac

Use this Rule to collect reminders or ideas in a plain text file while another app is open. The note comes from an input dialog, so you can write a new thought rather than needing to select existing text.

**When:** Type `;note` with exact case matching. **Do:** Ask for Input, append the answer to `~/Documents/Quick Notes.txt`, then show a notification. Each entry contains a bullet, the entered text, the current date and time, and a newline. There is no If Condition; cancelling the input stops the Rule.

## Configure and try it

1. Import with **Open this Rule in Rulr** and choose a typed trigger you do not normally use in documents.
2. Select a writable notes file in Write to File. Keep append-to-end mode to retain earlier notes.
3. Allow Accessibility for Text Typed and Notifications for the completion message.
4. Enable the Rule, type the trigger in a normal text field, and submit a test note. Inspect the file, then add another note to check the entry separation. Try cancelling the dialog as well.

## Requirements and limits

Text Typed and Write to File require Rulr Pro. The completion notification depends on macOS notification settings; inspect the file to confirm the saved content.

This writes to a local text file, rather than creating an Apple Notes Quick Note. It does not capture a source URL or selected passage. For collecting existing passages, use [Save Selected Text](/rules/save-selected-text-mac/).

## Does each note replace the previous one?

Write to File uses append-to-end mode. The sample adds a bullet, your entered text, the current date and time, and a newline, keeping earlier entries in the same file. Leave append mode selected if you want one running notes file instead of replacing its contents.
rules.intro:
Take a quick note on Mac by typing a short trigger. Write your thought in a prompt and save it with a timestamp to a text file, ready for your next note.

The sample listens for `;note`, asks what you want to remember, writes your answer to the notes file, and shows a notification. Choose your own typed trigger and destination after importing.
requiredConfiguration: Choose a notes file
rules.title: Quick Note

rules.description: Recognize and copy text from anywhere on your Mac screen.
rules.documentation:
## Use screen OCR to copy text you cannot select

For an existing image, you may only need macOS Live Text.

Use this Rule for visible labels, screenshots, or application content that you cannot highlight as ordinary text. It recognizes text from the configured screen capture target and copies the result so you can paste it into a note, message, or document.

**When:** Press the configured hotkey, initially Option + Space. **Do:** Recognize Text on Screen, then set the clipboard to the recognized Text output. There is no If Condition. The sample capture target is a full screen; it does not automatically limit recognition to the sentence or control you are looking at.

## Configure and try it

1. Import with **Open this Rule in Rulr** and choose a shortcut that is not already assigned to another Rule or app.
2. Review the capture target in Recognize Text on Screen. Choose the supported screen or area settings that fit the content you want.
3. Grant Screen Recording access when requested. Accessibility access is needed if you record a replacement shortcut.
4. Display a short, clearly readable sentence, run the Rule, and paste into a temporary document. Compare the copied text with the screen before using it elsewhere.

For image files arriving in a folder, choose [Extract Text from New Images](/rules/extract-text-images-mac/) instead of capturing the screen. The [Recognize Text on Screen Action](/capabilities/actions/#action.image.recognize-text-on-screen) lists the capture input and output; the [Mac automation guide](/posts/mac-automation/) explains how to connect that output to another step.

## Requirements and limits

The sample's Actions are available without Pro. Screen Recording permission is needed even though the result is text rather than a saved screenshot.

OCR can misread small text, unusual fonts, or complex layouts and may capture other visible text within the target. The clipboard result replaces its previous text; it does not automatically paste or translate it. For translation after recognition, see [Translate Screen Text](/rules/translate-screen-text-mac/).

## Screen OCR or image-file OCR?

Choose this Rule when the text is already visible on screen, including an image opened in another app. For automatically reading new image files as they arrive in a folder, use [Extract Text from New Images](/rules/extract-text-images-mac/). This screen workflow does not scan a folder or turn a multipage PDF into a searchable document.

{{< published-post-link path="/posts/ocr-for-mac-images-screenshots" label="Compare Live Text, screen OCR, and image-file OCR on Mac" >}}
rules.intro:
Copy text from images, screenshots, or apps visible on your Mac screen with one keyboard shortcut. OCR reads the text and puts it on your clipboard.

The sample recognizes the full screen, then copies the recognized Text output. Review the capture target and shortcut after importing; the result is ready to paste into your notes or document.
rules.title: Copy Text from Your Screen

rules.description: Mute audio and close private apps automatically when your Mac is idle.
rules.documentation:
## Quiet selected apps after inactivity

This Rule is useful when you regularly step away from your Mac and want audio silent with selected communication apps closed. It provides a small away routine based on inactivity rather than a fixed clock time or a manually pressed shortcut.

**When:** The Mac reaches 30 minutes of idle time. **Do:** Set system volume to zero, quit Messages, and quit Mail. There is no If Condition. These are explicit Actions: the sample does not inspect which apps contain private information or choose them automatically.

## Configure and try it

1. Import using **Open this Rule in Rulr** and review the idle duration and its unit. Set the interval that fits your normal breaks.
2. Review both Quit Application Actions. Select the apps you want to close or remove a step if hiding or leaving that app running is more appropriate.
3. Test with saved or disposable work and quiet audio. You can temporarily shorten the interval, then leave the Mac untouched until the Trigger runs.
4. Check the system volume and app states, and restore the intended interval after testing. Review whether normal quit prompts prevent either app from closing.

## Requirements and limits

The sample's components are available without Pro and declare no special permission. The selected apps must be installed, and the audio output must support the system volume change.

This routine does not lock the screen, clear notifications, erase message history, or guarantee that an app quits despite unsaved work. It also has no return-from-idle branch to restore volume or reopen apps. For quitting a single app at a particular time, see [Quit App on Schedule](/rules/quit-app-on-schedule-mac/).
rules.intro:
Mute your Mac and close private apps automatically after a period of inactivity, keeping Messages and Mail out of view and audio silent when you step away.

Lock Screen or more Quit Application Actions can extend the idle flow into a fuller away mode or privacy cleanup routine.
rules.title: Mute and Close Apps When Idle

rules.description: Open the right Chrome research workspace for each work session.
rules.documentation:
## Choose research tabs by session time

This Rule opens different Chrome pages for research and writing sessions. It demonstrates time Conditions after a keyboard Trigger, so the same shortcut can lead to different destinations without maintaining separate shortcuts for every session.

**When:** The configured hotkey is pressed. **Do:** Activate Chrome. **If:** The current time falls within 08:00–12:00, open Google Scholar and Notion; within 13:00–18:00, open Google Docs and Drive. Each matching branch also shows its session notification. Outside both intervals, Chrome is activated but neither tab group opens.

## Configure and try it

1. Import through **Open this Rule in Rulr**. Review and record the intended shortcut in the app before relying on the sample's displayed key label.
2. Adjust both start and end Conditions in each branch. Keep the paired Conditions together so each branch describes a time interval.
3. Replace the example URLs and notification text with your research and writing destinations. Allow Accessibility for Chrome activation, Automation for Chrome tabs, and Notifications for system alerts.
4. Test during a matching interval, or temporarily adjust its boundaries to include the current time. Confirm that only the intended group opens, then restore your preferred hours.

The time Conditions choose a tab group after you press the shortcut; they do not start a session at a scheduled hour. Compare [Open Chrome Work Tabs](/rules/open-chrome-work-tabs-mac/) if every session should open the same URLs. See [Variables](/capabilities/variables/) for current-time checks and the [AI Builder refinement walkthrough](/posts/build-mac-automations-with-ai/#4-refine-the-rule-through-conversation) for reviewing a change to allowed hours.

## Requirements and limits

The sample's Trigger and Actions do not require Pro. Notifications are shown when Rulr is not frontmost and may also be affected by macOS notification settings.

This is a manually triggered workspace, not a scheduled launcher. Repeating the shortcut opens additional tabs. It does not restore a previous browser session or identify research pages automatically. For a fixed set without time branches, use [Open Chrome Work Tabs](/rules/open-chrome-work-tabs-mac/).
rules.intro:
Open a Chrome research workspace with a keyboard shortcut, then load different research or writing tabs automatically based on the time of day.

The time-based branches can open different source URLs or lead into more Actions, extending the Rule into a writing setup, project launcher, or daily reading routine.

rules.description: Translate copied text and show the result.
rules.documentation:
## Automatically translate text copied to your Mac clipboard

This Rule suits a reading session in which you repeatedly copy unfamiliar text. Its input comes from the clipboard event, so you do not need a separate Get Selected Text Action or a hotkey for each passage.

**When:** The clipboard changes. **Do:** Translate the event's text to English, then show the translated output as text. There is no If Condition to restrict the source app or skip particular content.

## Configure and try it

1. Import using **Open this Rule in Rulr** and choose the target language in Translate Text.
2. Complete the Translation Shortcut setup requested by Rulr before enabling the Rule.
3. Copy a short passage in another language and check the displayed translation. Copy a different passage to verify a second run.
4. Disable the Rule when you finish the reading session if you do not want ordinary copying to trigger it.

## Requirements and limits

Clipboard Changed requires Rulr Pro. Translate Text requires the Translation Shortcut dependency; supported languages and translation availability depend on that setup.

The sample handles text. It does not perform image OCR, save clipboard history, or replace the clipboard with the translation. Non-text clipboard changes may provide no useful text to translate. For translation only when you request it, use [Translate Selected Text](/rules/translate-selected-text-mac/); for text inside images, use [Translate Screen Text](/rules/translate-screen-text-mac/).

## Can I paste the translated text immediately?

The sample shows the translation in a result panel but leaves the clipboard unchanged. A normal paste still uses the original copied text. Choose this Rule for reading translations while copying passages; automatic translated-text insertion would require a different flow, including a guard against triggering another run when the clipboard changes.
rules.intro:
Translate clipboard text automatically on Mac whenever you copy a passage. Choose the target language and see the translation without a separate hotkey.

Clipboard Changed passes the copied text to Translate Text, which targets English in the sample. Change the target language after importing and enable the Rule when you want clipboard-driven translation.

Allow Accessibility for app activation, then launch the meeting app with each output selected and check the result.

rules.documentation:
## Sort incoming photos and videos into separate folders

Use this Rule for a folder that receives mixed media exports or downloads. Both branches use the path from the folder event, so each move applies to the arriving item rather than a fixed example file.

**When:** An item is added to `~/Downloads`. **If:** Its name matches PNG, JPG, JPEG, HEIC, or WebP, **Do:** Move it to `~/Pictures/Media`. A separate branch matches MOV, MP4, or M4V and moves it to `~/Movies/Imports`. Both regular expressions ignore case and match the end of the filename.

## Configure and try it

1. Import through **Open this Rule in Rulr** and choose the folder that receives your media files.
2. Select existing, writable destination folders in both Move Actions. Keep destinations separate from the watched source.
3. Review the extension patterns and numbered-name conflict policy. The Actions move files out of the source.
4. Enable the Rule and add disposable image and video copies. Check each destination, then add an unsupported file type to confirm it stays in the source. Try a duplicate filename as well.

## Requirements and limits

Folder Contents Changed and Move File or Folder require Rulr Pro. Rulr needs access to the source and destinations.

The Rule routes files by name; it does not inspect media contents, sort by capture date, convert formats, or import into the Photos library. Existing files are not a backfill job, and no explicit wait for unfinished downloads is configured. For routing PDFs and archives alongside images, see [Sort Downloads](/rules/sort-downloads-mac/).

## Does this organize the Apple Photos library?

It moves ordinary files between folders in Finder. It does not create Photos albums, read EXIF capture dates, or scan the existing photo library. Choose this workflow for separating incoming image files from video files before reviewing or importing them elsewhere.
rules.intro:
Automatically separate new photos and videos into different folders on Mac. Watch one incoming folder and move matching media files by their extensions.

rules.description: Move the focused window to the left half of its screen with a shortcut.
rules.documentation:
## Arrange the focused window

Replacing an AutoHotkey `WinMove` shortcut? The [AutoHotkey for Mac guide](/posts/autohotkey-for-mac/) explains how to rebuild window hotkeys and what to change when selecting Mac windows and screens.

**When:** Press Option + Left Arrow. **Do:** Set Window Layout for the focused window using the left-half preset. There is no If Condition.

## Configure and try it

1. Import the Rule and review its Option + Left Arrow shortcut. Choose an unused combination if it conflicts with another app.
2. Grant Accessibility access to Rulr and enable the Rule.
3. Focus a window in another app, then press the shortcut. The window moves and resizes to the left half of its current screen's visible area.
4. To use a different arrangement, choose another preset in Set Window Layout.

## Requirements and limits

This Rule requires a Rulr version with Set Window Layout and Accessibility access. The target app must expose a window that can be moved and resized. Some windows may not support the requested dimensions, and full-screen windows are not supported.

The Rule snaps the focused window to the left half when the shortcut is pressed. It does not continuously arrange other windows, provide drag-to-snap controls, or restore a saved workspace. For a comparison of these approaches, see the [Mac window manager guide](/posts/window-manager-mac/).

For a presentation on another monitor, [Present New Video Windows](/rules/full-screen-keyboard-shortcut-mac/) reacts to new windows from your selected video app, moving each event's window to your configured display before toggling full screen.
rules.intro:
Move and resize the focused window to the left half of your Mac screen with a keyboard shortcut. Use this Rule when you want a simple, repeatable window layout.

The Rule uses Set Window Layout with Focused Window and the left-half preset. Change the shortcut or choose another layout after importing.

rules.description: Open a panel of detected media sources and play or pause eligible players.
rules.documentation:
## Choose which media source to control

When music, videos, and browser tabs are spread across your Mac, opening each player to pause or resume it interrupts what you are doing. This Rule opens Rulr's Media Manager so you can choose a detected source and use the panel's play/pause control.

The panel shows available titles alongside app names. Supported browser media pages appear as separate entries. Sources remembered after playback can remain in the list when paused, so you can return to them without starting playback again first.

**When:** Press Option + M. **If:** No Condition. **Do:** Show Media Manager. Opening the panel does not itself pause or resume anything. Click a row or use Up and Down to select it, press Space to request play/pause, and press Escape to dismiss the panel.

## Configure and try it

1. Choose **Open this Rule in Rulr** on a Mac running macOS 26 or later. Review the imported Rule, which starts disabled.
2. Keep Option + M or choose an unused shortcut in Hotkey Pressed. Show Media Manager has no parameters to configure.
3. Allow Accessibility for the hotkey, then enable the Rule. Start a song or video in an app or Chrome tab you use regularly.
4. Open the panel while the song or video is actually playing, and wait for its source to appear before pausing it. Select that source. If the panel requests access for playback, follow its permission guidance. Press Space and check that the selected player actually pauses; press it again to check resuming.
5. Try a second source and repeat with both players open. Confirm the behavior for your own apps before relying on the Rule during work or calls.

For Chrome tab discovery and control, allow Rulr to automate Google Chrome and enable **View → Developer → Allow JavaScript from Apple Events** in Chrome. Safari tab discovery also requires its Automation and JavaScript permissions, but Safari playback control is currently unavailable. Native playback may require Accessibility; controlling individual QuickTime movies can require QuickTime Player Automation access.

## Compatibility and limits

Media Manager is available without Pro. The source list itself does not capture audio or require recording permission. The shortcut and some playback paths have separate permission requirements.

Discovery, title display, and playback control are separate capabilities. An entry appearing in the panel does not guarantee that Rulr can control it. Native apps differ in the media sessions and playback controls they expose; there is no claim of compatibility with every player or version.

Chrome control uses accessible media elements on the selected page. Embedded players, custom players, and other page designs may not be discoverable or controllable. A browser page generally needs to be observed playing before it is retained after pausing; a page that was already paused before discovery may be absent. Temporarily unreadable sources can show their last confirmed state.

Remembered sources belong to the current Rulr session; this is not a persistent playback history. Quitting the source app or closing a discovered browser page can remove its entry.

If your app is not detected or cannot be controlled, contact [support@rulr.app](mailto:support@rulr.app) with the app name, version, and what happens when you try.

This Rule opens an interactive picker. It does not bind the hardware media keys to a chosen app, choose a player automatically for those keys, or provide next/previous-track controls.

Read [Show Media Manager](/capabilities/actions/#action.system.show-media-manager) for the Action, or use [Switch Audio Output](/rules/switch-audio-output-mac/) when your goal is changing speakers or headphones rather than controlling playback.

{{< published-post-link path="/posts/mac-media-playback-control/" label="Media playback control on Mac: explore a unified panel and compare BeardedSpice alternatives." >}}
rules.intro:
Open a Mac media control panel with Option + M. See detected music and video sources, select a player, and press Space to play or pause when control is available.

The Rule connects Hotkey Pressed to Show Media Manager with no Conditions or Action parameters. Replace the shortcut to suit your keyboard; source discovery and playback control depend on the app, browser, and permissions.
requiredConfiguration: Choose an unused shortcut and allow permissions needed by your players.
rules.title: Media Manager

rules.description: Search and switch between open Chrome windows and tabs.
rules.documentation:
## Find a page across Chrome windows

When research, documentation, and project tabs are spread across several Chrome windows, it can be hard to remember where a page is open. This Rule gives you one keyboard shortcut to open Rulr's searchable Chrome window and tab manager, so you can find a page and switch to it without checking each window separately.

**When:** Press Option + Space, the shortcut included in this Rule. **Do:** Open the Chrome window and tab manager. There is no If condition in this sample, so the shortcut runs the Action directly. The manager also offers controls to create, reload, or close Chrome windows and tabs; opening the Rule does not automatically perform those operations.

## Set up and test

1. Use **Open this Rule in Rulr** above to import the Rule into the app on your Mac.
2. Review the **Hotkey Pressed** Trigger. The default is Option + Space; choose another shortcut if you already use it for a launcher or another app.
3. Allow Rulr to control **Google Chrome** when macOS requests Automation permission. If you record a different shortcut, grant **Accessibility** access for shortcut recording. You can review both permissions under **System Settings → Privacy & Security**.
4. Open a few Chrome tabs in more than one window, and make sure the Rule is enabled in Rulr. Press your chosen shortcut to open the manager.
5. Search for a page you have open and select it. Confirm that Chrome switches to the intended tab and window. Repeat with a page in another window to check the workflow you will use day to day.

Choose this Rule for a page that is already open. Use [Open Chrome Work Tabs](/rules/open-chrome-work-tabs-mac/) for a fixed set of destinations, or [Chrome Research Workspace](/rules/chrome-research-workspace/) when the destination group depends on the time. The [Show Window and Tab Manager Action](/capabilities/actions/#action.integration.chrome.show-window-and-tab-manager) lists the component requirements. For combining browser tasks with other steps, see the [Mac automation guide](/posts/mac-automation/).

## Requirements and limits

This sample is for Google Chrome on Mac. It does not search Safari tabs, browsing history, bookmarks, or the contents of every webpage. It helps you navigate windows and tabs that are already open; it does not save or restore a browser session.

The Action has no parameters to fill in, so the main setup choices are the shortcut and required permissions. If the manager does not open, check that the Rule is enabled and the shortcut is not assigned elsewhere. If you cannot record a replacement shortcut, review Accessibility access. If Chrome cannot be controlled, review its Automation permission for Rulr.

For a different task, such as opening a fixed set of research pages, browse the [web and browsing Rules](/rules/web-browsing/). You can also [explore Rulr's capabilities](/capabilities/) before extending this Rule with additional Actions.
rules.intro:
Search open Chrome windows and tabs from one Mac keyboard shortcut, then switch directly to the page you need without scanning every browser window.

This starting point can be extended with Chrome Actions that open, close, or navigate tabs for research, focused reading, or client workflows.
rules.title: Chrome Window Manager

rules.description: Back up matching project downloads to a separate folder.
rules.documentation:
## Automatically copy matching files between Mac folders

Use this Rule for project exports or deliveries that need a second local copy. It copies rather than moves the matching item, so the original remains available in the source folder.

**When:** An item is added or renamed in `~/Downloads`. **If:** The event's filename contains `Project`. **Do:** Copy File to `~/Documents/Project Backups`, using a numbered name if the destination name already exists. The two Triggers feed the same matching and copy path.

## Configure and try it

1. Import with **Open this Rule in Rulr** and set the watched folder in both the added and renamed Triggers.
2. Replace `Project` with the filename text that identifies the files you want to copy.
3. Select an existing writable backup folder outside the watched source and review the name-conflict policy.
4. Enable the Rule and add a disposable matching file. Confirm the original remains and the copy appears. Rename a test item to a matching name, then try a nonmatching name to check both event paths and the filter.

## Requirements and limits

Folder Contents Changed requires Rulr Pro; Copy File itself is available without Pro. Rulr needs access to both folders.

This is an event-driven extra copy, with no explicit wait for a file still being written. It is not a full backup system: there is no version retention, deletion propagation, existing-folder scan, or monitoring of later content edits. Repeated matching events can create additional numbered copies. For triggering your own processing instead, see [Run Shortcut for Folder](/rules/watch-folder-run-shortcut-mac/).

## Does this keep two folders in sync?

It makes an extra copy when a matching item arrives or is renamed. Editing the original later does not update the copy, and deleting the original does not delete its copy. Use the Rule for incoming project deliveries that need a second copy, rather than continuous folder synchronization.
rules.intro:
Automatically copy matching new files to another folder on Mac while keeping the originals. Choose a watched folder, filename filter, and backup destination.

The sample watches Downloads, matches names containing `Project`, and copies each matching event path to a separate destination. Choose your source, name filter, and backup folder after importing.

rules.documentation:
## Use one input source in selected apps

This Rule changes the keyboard input source when you switch into particular applications. It is useful when your browser or design tools should use a predictable typing layout regardless of what you were using in the previous app.

**When:** The frontmost application changes. **If:** The new app is Safari, Google Chrome, or Figma. **Do:** Switch the input source to ABC. The application Conditions use OR matching, so any listed app starts the same Action. The sample does not assign a different language to each app.

## Configure and try it

1. Import with **Open this Rule in Rulr** and replace or remove the application Conditions to match the apps you use.
2. Select an input source installed on your Mac in Switch Input Method. The sample identifier represents Apple's ABC keyboard layout.
3. Keep OR matching when any one of the listed applications should trigger the switch. Use separate branches or Rules if different apps need different input sources.
4. Enable the Rule, switch to a different input source, and activate one matching app. Check the macOS input indicator and type in a temporary field. Repeat with an app outside the list.

## Requirements and limits

The sample's Trigger and Action are available without Pro and declare no special permission. The chosen input source must already be installed and enabled on the Mac.

The Rule switches the system's active input source; it does not translate text, change a document's language, or restore the previous input source when you leave the matched app. It runs on application changes rather than individual text-field focus. For inserting a reusable phrase, see [Text Expansion](/rules/text-expansion-mac/).

Automatically switch your Mac input method or input source by app, such as using English in a code editor and Chinese in a messaging app.

Choose the applications and installed keyboard input source after importing the Rule. Add or replace application Conditions when different apps should switch the Mac keyboard language automatically.

rules.documentation:
## How this Rule works

The hotkey starts Get Current Tab in Google Chrome, then Write to File appends the resulting URL. There is no Condition, page title, or separator configured in the sample.

## Configure and try it

Choose a shortcut and a writable destination file. Allow Accessibility and Automation access to Google Chrome, enable the Rule, open a Chrome page, and press the shortcut. Inspect the file; if you want entries separated by newlines, add a newline to the write content.

## Requirements and limits

rules.description: Open tools for the current session after joining the office network.
rules.documentation:
## Launch work apps when you connect to a Wi-Fi network

This Rule combines a network event with two time-based branches. It is useful when arriving at a workplace means opening a predictable set of apps, and your morning and afternoon routines differ.

**When:** A network connects. **If:** Its SSID equals `Office`. From 08:00 inclusive to 12:00 exclusive, **Do:** Launch Slack and Notion, then open Google Calendar in Safari. From 13:00 inclusive to 18:00 exclusive, launch Slack and Figma, then open Notion's website in Safari. Each time window uses AND Conditions.

## Configure and try it

1. Import with **Open this Rule in Rulr** and replace `Office` with your Wi-Fi network's SSID.
2. Choose installed apps and the public or personal work URLs you intend to open. Review both branches separately.
3. Adjust the time boundaries for your local routine. There is no weekday Condition in this sample.
4. Enable the Rule and reconnect to the chosen network during a matching time window. Check the expected apps and pages; try a different network to check the SSID filter.

## Requirements and limits

The sample's components are available without Pro and declare no special permission. Websites still require any normal sign-in.

The network event must provide an SSID matching the Condition. Joining another network or connecting outside both windows launches nothing. Crossing 08:00 or 13:00 while already connected does not itself trigger the Rule. Reconnecting may launch the tools again. For a time-driven routine, see [Launch Apps at a Scheduled Time](/rules/launch-apps-at-time-mac/).

## Can I use my home Wi-Fi instead of office Wi-Fi?

Replace `Office` with your home network's SSID, then choose the apps, pages, and time windows you need. The Rule uses a network-name match, not your physical location. It does not connect to Wi-Fi for you or wait for website sign-in to finish.
rules.intro:
Open apps and websites automatically when your Mac joins a chosen Wi-Fi network. Set morning and afternoon app groups for your office or home work routine.

Set your network name, apps, URLs, and working hours after importing. The sample checks the connected SSID, then opens the tools for the matching time window.
requiredConfiguration: Choose an office network, work hours, applications, and URLs

rules.description: Arrange a selected app window when an external monitor connects.
rules.documentation:
## Move an app window after a display change

This Rule helps place a frequently used application on another screen when your display setup changes. It is useful for a desk routine where connecting an external monitor should move one working window to a preferred display.

**When:** The display layout changes. **If:** The event reports more than one connected display. **Do:** Move the selected application's last-used window to the configured screen. The sample application is Safari and the screen value is `1`; review both on your own Mac rather than assuming that number identifies the monitor you want.

## Configure and try it

1. Import with **Open this Rule in Rulr** and select the application in Move Window to Screen.
2. Choose the intended screen from your connected display setup and review the last-used window selection. Open a window in that app before testing.
3. Grant Accessibility access so Rulr can move application windows. Enable the Rule, then connect your monitor or make a display-layout change.
4. Confirm which window moved and where it landed. Repeat after reconnecting the display, especially if you use several docks or different monitor arrangements.

Use this event-driven Rule for one window's display placement, and [Window Switcher](/rules/mac-window-switcher/) for manually choosing an existing window. The [Display Layout Changed Trigger](/capabilities/#trigger.system.display-layout-changed) exposes the display event; [Move Window to Screen](/capabilities/actions/#action.window.move-to-screen) defines the movement. The [Mac automation guide](/posts/mac-automation/#how-rulr-automates-your-mac) explains why the display-count Condition sits between them.

## Requirements and limits

The display-layout Trigger and window-moving Action require Rulr Pro. The target application must have a movable window, and the selected screen must be available when the Action runs.

The Trigger covers layout changes rather than one particular monitor's connection. A rearrangement can therefore run the Rule again whenever more than one display is present. The sample moves one selected window; it does not resize it, tile every app, or manage Spaces. For choosing among existing windows manually, use [Window Switcher](/rules/mac-window-switcher/).

For built-in tiling and other ways to arrange windows, see the [Mac window manager comparison](/posts/window-manager-mac/).
rules.intro:
Automatically move one app window to your chosen display when an external monitor connects to your Mac.

The Rule runs when the display layout changes, checks that more than one display is connected, and moves the selected app's last-used window to the target screen. Choose the application and display after importing it.

rules.description: Process entered text with AppleScript and show the result.
rules.documentation:
## Pass entered text through AppleScript

This Rule demonstrates a text input flowing through a script and into a result panel. It is a base for a small formatter or converter when you want to review script output before deciding where to use it.

**When:** Press Option + R. **Do:** Ask for text, pass that input to Run AppleScript, and display the script's result. There is no If Condition. The supplied script simply returns its first argument unchanged; it does not yet format, validate, or convert the text.

## Configure and try it

1. Import with **Open this Rule in Rulr**, then review the hotkey and the input prompt. Change the prompt to describe your actual AppleScript task; the sample prompt still mentions a shell script.
2. Review the script and its input Variable. Keep the prompted value connected to the script input and the returned result connected to Show Text or Image.
3. Try the unchanged sample first by entering a short sentence. Confirm that the panel displays the same sentence. Cancel a second prompt and verify that processing stops.
4. Replace the script with your intended transformation and test representative input. Review the 30-second timeout if the script performs a longer task.

## Requirements and limits

The sample's components are available without Pro. Accessibility is needed if you record a replacement shortcut. A different script may require additional Automation permissions depending on the apps it controls.

The sample asks for input; it does not read the current selection or run a shell command. Script failure stops the flow before result display. For saving selected passages directly, use [Save Selected Text](/rules/save-selected-text-mac/).

To run an existing compiled script on a schedule, use [Schedule AppleScript File](/rules/run-scpt-file-mac/) and configure its actual file path. For native text processing, compare [Remove Emoji from Text](/rules/remove-emojis-from-text-mac/) and [Extract Line-End Number](/rules/remove-line-breaks-regex-mac/).

For an implemented alphabet-position conversion, [Letters and Alphabet Positions](/rules/letters-to-numbers-mac/) converts A–Z to 1–26 and back, with input checks and a result panel.
rules.intro:
Process text with AppleScript on your Mac from a keyboard shortcut, passing entered text into a script and displaying the returned result when it finishes.

Another AppleScript can send its result through Set Clipboard to Text, Insert Text, or Write to File, creating a formatter, validator, converter, or other text-processing tool.

rules.description: Prepare a distraction-free workspace and track one work block.
rules.documentation:
## Start a focus timer and prepare your Mac workspace

Use this Rule to combine the setup and ending reminder for a focused writing or study period. A confirmation dialog comes before the app-closing Actions, so you can cancel without starting the session.

**When:** Press Option + F. **Do:** Ask for confirmation, quit Messages and Mail, open `~/Documents`, launch TextEdit, delay for 50 minutes, and show a completion notification with sound. There is no If Condition and no repeating work/break cycle.

## Configure and try it

1. Import using **Open this Rule in Rulr** and choose the shortcut. Review both Quit Application Actions before running the sample.
2. Select your work folder and writing or study app. Save work in apps you intend to close.
3. Adjust the Delay duration and update the confirmation text to match. Allow Accessibility for the hotkey and Notifications for the reminder.
4. Temporarily use a short delay to try the sequence. Check cancellation first, then confirm a session and inspect the setup and final notification. Restore your intended duration afterward.

## Requirements and limits

The sample's components are available without Pro. Rulr must keep running for the delayed notification, whose visibility and sound also depend on macOS settings.

This Rule quits the selected apps once; it does not block them from reopening, enable macOS Focus, or display a live countdown. It does not reopen the closed apps when the session ends. For closing an app at a fixed clock time, see [Quit an App on a Schedule](/rules/quit-app-on-schedule-mac/).

## Can I use a 25-minute focus session?

Change Delay to 25 minutes and update the confirmation message to match. The completion notification follows that delay. This times one work block; it does not automatically start a break or repeat a Pomodoro cycle.
rules.intro:
Start a focus timer on Mac with a keyboard shortcut. Confirm, close distracting apps, open your work folder, and get a reminder after your chosen work block.

The sample uses a 50-minute delay after opening Documents and TextEdit. Choose which apps to quit, your working folder, and the session length before enabling it.

rules.description: Launch an app and bring it forward from one shortcut.
rules.documentation:
## Create a keyboard shortcut to launch a Mac app

Use this Rule for an app you return to throughout the day, such as a browser or editor. The explicit activation Action brings the target app forward after the launch request.

Moving an app-launch hotkey from Windows? The [AutoHotkey for Mac migration guide](/posts/autohotkey-for-mac/) maps a hotkey followed by `Run` to this launch-and-focus workflow and compares other Mac alternatives.

**When:** Press Option + Space. **Do:** Launch Application, then Make Application Frontmost, both targeting Google Chrome. There is no If Condition, time restriction, or show/hide toggle.

## Configure and try it

1. Import through **Open this Rule in Rulr** and replace Option + Space if it conflicts with an existing shortcut or another Rule.
2. Choose an installed app in Launch Application and select the same app in Make Application Frontmost.
3. Grant Accessibility for the hotkey and frontmost Action.
4. Enable the Rule and test once with the app closed. Switch to another app and test again with the target already running; check that it comes forward.

## Requirements and limits

The sample's components are available without Pro. The target application must be installed and launchable by the current Mac user.

The Rule targets one application. It does not select a particular document, create a new window, or search among open windows. To hide the same app on a second press, use [Toggle App Visibility](/rules/toggle-app-visibility-mac/). To open several apps together with time Conditions, use [Open Work Apps](/rules/open-work-apps-mac/).

## What happens if the app is already open?

The Rule sends the launch request and then makes the selected application frontmost. Both Actions should target the same app. Pressing the shortcut again brings that app forward; it does not hide it or toggle between two apps.

If you are choosing an automation tool, [compare this launch-and-focus task in two tools](/posts/keyboard-maestro-alternative/#the-same-task-in-both-tools-launch-and-focus-an-app), including their configuration and run-inspection differences.

For more tasks you can start with a hotkey or another event, see the [Mac macro software guide](/posts/mac-macro-software/). It compares automation tools and uses this launch-and-focus Rule as one example alongside system, file, and text tasks.
rules.intro:
Open an app with a keyboard shortcut on Mac and bring it to the front. Pick your app and hotkey to launch it or return to it while working elsewhere.

The sample launches Google Chrome and then makes it frontmost. Select the same app in both Actions and choose a shortcut that fits your keyboard setup.
requiredConfiguration: Choose a shortcut and application
rules.title: Launch and Focus App

rules.description: Close related tools when the main work app quits.

## How this Rule works

When Safari quits, two Quit Application Actions target Notes and TextEdit. There is no Condition, and this does not watch individual windows or determine which documents belong to a project.

## Configure and try it

Choose the main app in the Trigger and replace both companion apps with your own. Save work in those apps, enable the Rule, open them, and quit the main app. Confirm the intended apps receive the quit request.

## Requirements and limits

The Trigger and Actions do not require Pro or declare special permissions. An app can prompt about unsaved documents or otherwise delay quitting; this Rule does not save documents for you.

rules.description: Open a selected project folder when its working app launches.
rules.documentation:
## Open a folder when your working app launches

This Rule pairs an application's launch with the folder you usually need next. For example, starting a writing app can open your reference folder so project documents are available without navigating through Finder each time.

**When:** The selected application launches. **Do:** Open a configured folder using the default application. There is no If Condition. The sample watches TextEdit and opens Downloads; those are starting values to replace with the app and project location on your Mac.

## Configure and try it

1. Import with **Open this Rule in Rulr**, then select the application in the launch Trigger. Use the installed app you actually start for the project.
2. Choose the project folder in Open File or Folder. Review the opening application: Default normally lets macOS decide, while a specific compatible app can provide a different result.
3. Enable the Rule, save any work, quit the selected application, and launch it again. Check that the chosen folder opens.
4. Switch away from the app and back without quitting it. This should not be treated as another launch event; choose an activation Trigger instead if that is the workflow you want.

## Requirements and limits

The selected app must be installed and the folder must exist with access available to Rulr. The sample's components are available without Pro and declare no additional special permission.

Opening a folder does not automatically load a particular editor workspace, start a development server, or restore project windows. Those tasks need their own supported Actions. To start several applications together from a keyboard shortcut, see [Open Work Apps](/rules/open-work-apps-mac/).
rules.intro:
Automatically open a project folder when a selected editor, terminal, or other working app launches on your Mac.

requiredConfiguration: Choose a working app
