rules.description: Show or hide a selected application with the same shortcut.
rules.documentation:
## Show or hide one app with the same shortcut

This Rule gives a frequently used application its own visibility shortcut. It is useful for keeping a reference browser or utility available when needed, then moving its windows out of view without quitting the app.

**When:** Press the configured hotkey, initially Option + Space. **Do:** Toggle the selected application's visibility. There is no If Condition. The sample targets Safari: a visible application is hidden, while a hidden application is shown.

## Configure and try it

1. Import with **Open this Rule in Rulr** and select the application in Toggle Application Visibility. Choose an app installed on your Mac rather than leaving Safari unless that is your intended target.
2. Review the hotkey and assign a unique combination. Several Gallery samples use Option + Space, so change it when combining them.
3. Grant Accessibility if you need to record the replacement shortcut. Launch the target application and open an ordinary window before testing.
4. Press the shortcut and check that the app hides. Press it again and verify that it reappears with its existing work. Try the routine from another frontmost app as well.

## Requirements and limits

Toggle Application Visibility requires Rulr Pro. The Action itself declares no additional special permission, though recording a shortcut uses Accessibility access.

Hiding is an application visibility change. It does not close documents, quit the app, silence its audio, or prevent notifications. The sample also has no separate Launch Application Action; test with a running app rather than treating this as a launcher. For choosing among several open application windows, use [Window Switcher](/rules/mac-window-switcher/).
rules.intro:
Use one keyboard shortcut to show or hide a selected running app on your Mac, keeping its windows available without quitting the app or closing documents.

Choose the application and hotkey after importing the Rule. The Action changes visibility without quitting the app or closing its windows.
requiredConfiguration: Choose a shortcut and application
rules.title: Toggle App Visibility

rules.description: Send a configured key sequence after a selected application launches.
rules.documentation:
## Send a shortcut after an app starts

This Rule is useful when opening an application is regularly followed by the same keyboard command. It combines a launch event, application activation, a brief delay, and a recorded key sequence into one routine.

**When:** The selected app launches. **Do:** Bring that app forward, wait one second, and press the configured keys. There is no If Condition. The sample watches TextEdit and sends Command + S, so its visible result depends on the document and save state at the time of the keypress.

## Configure and try it

1. Import through **Open this Rule in Rulr** and choose your application in both the launch Trigger and Activate Application Action.
2. Record or select the intended key sequence in Type Text or Press Keys. Confirm that the same shortcut performs your desired command when pressed manually in that app.
3. Review the delay. One second is a starting value, not a guarantee that a document or network workspace has finished loading. Grant Accessibility access for activation and key simulation.
4. Save your work, quit the selected app, and relaunch it for a controlled test. Check which window receives the command and adjust the sequence or delay if needed.

## Requirements and limits

The key-simulation Action requires Rulr Pro. The selected application must be installed, and its keyboard command must be available in the active context.

The Rule responds to a launch rather than every switch back to an already running app. Another app taking focus during the delay can also affect input. It does not identify controls by name or verify that the command succeeded. For opening a project location on launch instead, see [Open Project Folder](/rules/open-project-folder-mac/).
rules.intro:
Automatically press a configured key or keyboard shortcut after a selected application launches on your Mac.

Choose the app and recorded key sequence after importing the Rule. It brings the application forward before sending the keys, so the result depends on the app's active window and current keyboard shortcuts.
requiredConfiguration: Choose an application and recorded key sequence
rules.title: Press Keys When an App Launches

rules.description: Move the pointer and click a configured position when a matching window opens.
rules.documentation:
## Click a position in a newly created window

Use this Rule for an application window whose useful control appears in a stable position. It moves the pointer relative to the window reported by the Trigger and performs a click there, reducing a repeated manual pointer movement.

**When:** The selected application creates a window. **If:** The event's application matches the configured app. **Do:** Move the pointer to the selected window-relative position, then click the current pointer location. The sample uses Safari, a 50% horizontal and 50% vertical position, and a single left click without modifiers.

## Configure and try it

1. Import with **Open this Rule in Rulr** and select the application in both the Trigger and application Condition.
2. Review Move Mouse. Keep its window source connected to the Trigger's Window Variable, then choose the percentage or coordinate position for your intended control.
3. Review the mouse button, click type, and modifiers in Click Mouse. Grant Accessibility access for window events and mouse control.
4. Test by opening a disposable window with a harmless target. Watch the pointer movement and resulting click before enabling the routine for normal work.

Before adapting this sample, compare its [Window Created Trigger](/capabilities/#trigger.application-window.window-created) and [Input Actions](/capabilities/actions/#actions-category-input) with the control you intend to click. If you ask AI Builder to change the target, follow the [review and testing walkthrough](/posts/build-mac-automations-with-ai/) and recheck the coordinates in the actual application; a generated change does not establish that the control is ready.

## Requirements and limits

The window-created Trigger and mouse Actions require Rulr Pro. Window detection depends on the application exposing a standard accessible window.

A coordinate points to a location, not a named button. Different window sizes, toolbars, loading states, or interface changes can place another control under it. The sample has no delay or readiness check before clicking. Recheck the target after app updates. For sending an application's keyboard shortcut after launch, see [Press Keys When an App Launches](/rules/press-keys-app-launch-mac/).
rules.intro:
Automatically move the pointer and click a configured position when a selected application window opens on your Mac.

Choose the application, window-relative position, mouse button, and click type after importing the Rule. Coordinate-based clicks can break when the window layout or application interface changes.
requiredConfiguration: Choose an application, window position, and click settings
rules.title: Click a Window Position

rules.description: Scroll a configured distance when a selected application becomes frontmost.
rules.documentation:
## Scroll when a selected app becomes active

This Rule is a starting point for a reading routine in which switching into an app should move its content down by a fixed amount. It first places the pointer inside the focused window so the scroll targets the area beneath that position.

**When:** The selected application becomes frontmost. **Do:** Move the pointer to the focused window's center, then scroll down by the configured distance. There is no If Condition. The sample selects Safari and uses a distance of 600; review the value in the app for your actual content and scrolling behavior.

## Configure and try it

1. Import with **Open this Rule in Rulr** and select the application in the activation Trigger.
2. Review Move Mouse. Its sample position is 50% across and 50% down the focused window. Choose a position over the content pane you want to scroll.
3. Set the scroll direction and distance, then grant Accessibility access for mouse movement and scrolling.
4. Open a harmless long document in the selected app, switch away, and switch back. Observe which pane scrolls and how far. Repeat with the layouts you normally use.

## Requirements and limits

The mouse and scrolling Actions require Rulr Pro. The app needs a focused window with scrollable content beneath the configured pointer position.

The Rule performs a scroll on activation; it does not continuously auto-scroll, wait until you finish reading, or recognize the end of an article. Every activation can scroll again. Sidebars, overlays, and embedded panes may receive the scroll instead of the main page. For another routine using window-relative pointer positioning, see [Click a Window Position](/rules/click-window-position-mac/).
rules.intro:
Automatically scroll a selected Mac application by a configured distance whenever it becomes frontmost.

Choose the application, pointer position, scroll direction, and distance after importing the Rule. The Rule moves the pointer into the target window before scrolling the content beneath it.
requiredConfiguration: Choose an application, pointer position, direction, and distance
rules.title: Scroll an App Automatically

rules.description: Prepare selected text for use in a URL.
rules.documentation:
## How this Rule works

When the shortcut is pressed, Get Selected Text feeds Transform Text with URL Encode selected. Set Clipboard then stores the transformed output. There is no Condition, automatic paste, or URL opening step.

## Configure and try it

Choose an unused shortcut, grant Accessibility and Automation access to System Events, then select a short phrase in a supported app. Press the shortcut and paste the clipboard into a text field to check the encoded result.

## Encode line breaks as %0A

A real line-feed character becomes `%0A` when URL encoded. Two line feeds become `%0A%0A`, which can represent paragraph spacing inside a URL parameter such as a prefilled message. Select the actual multi-line message, run the Rule, then use the encoded result as the parameter value.

For example, select these two lines with the actual line break between them:

```text
Hello
World
```

The encoded result is `Hello%0AWorld`. The line break becomes part of the parameter value instead of splitting the URL across two lines.

Literal `\n` is different from an actual line feed: the Rule encodes the characters you selected rather than interpreting them as a programming-language escape. Encoding text that already contains `%0A` also encodes its percent sign, producing `%250A`; do not encode the same value twice.

This Rule does not add a phone number, construct a WhatsApp URL or send a message. It provides the encoded text component for a URL you build separately.

## Requirements and limits

Transform Text requires Rulr Pro. Selection access depends on the frontmost app and macOS permissions. The Rule replaces the clipboard contents; it does not modify the selected text.
rules.intro:
URL encode selected text on Mac, including LF line breaks as %0A, and copy the result to the clipboard. The Rule reads the selection, transforms it, and copies the encoded text.

The sample uses Option-Space. Choose a shortcut that does not conflict with another app and select text in a supported app before running it.
rules.title: Encode Selected Text

rules.description: Hear selected text read aloud.
rules.documentation:
## Speak text from the current selection

This Rule is a starting point for listening to a passage while reviewing a document. It retrieves text exposed by the frontmost app and passes that text directly to speech, without first saving the passage in a separate file.

**When:** The exact typed phrase `;speak` is detected. **Do:** Get Selected Text, then Speak Text using the retrieved Text output. There is no If Condition. This is a typed Trigger rather than a keyboard shortcut in the supplied sample.

## Configure and try it

1. Import with **Open this Rule in Rulr** and review Text Typed. Choose a distinctive phrase if you keep this Trigger.
2. Grant Accessibility and System Events Automation access for selected-text retrieval. Accessibility also supports the typed Trigger.
3. Test with a short, nonessential selection in an application that exposes selected text. Observe whether entering the trigger phrase changes or replaces that selection before Rulr reads it.
4. If typing interferes with the selection in your app, replace Text Typed with Hotkey Pressed and test the selection again. Confirm that the speech matches the passage and that your audio output is audible.

## Requirements and limits

Text Typed and Speak Text require Rulr Pro. Reading a selection depends on application support, and some apps may briefly use the clipboard to retrieve it.

The sample speaks the text it actually retrieves; it does not automatically read a whole document, recognize words in an image, or translate the passage. Typed-trigger compatibility needs checking in each target app. For translating accessible selected text instead, see [Translate Selected Text](/rules/translate-selected-text-mac/).
rules.intro:
Type a configured trigger phrase on your Mac to retrieve selected text from a compatible frontmost app and read the passage aloud with Rulr.

Text Typed starts the Rule, Get Selected Text reads the selection from the frontmost application, and Speak Text reads it aloud. Choose a trigger phrase and use it with selected text in a compatible application.
rules.title: Speak Selected Text

rules.description: Trim copied research text and append it to your notes.
rules.documentation:
## How this Rule works

A Clipboard Changed Trigger supplies its text to Transform Text, which trims it. Write to File appends a bullet, the result, the current date and time, and a newline; a notification follows. There is no Condition to filter sensitive or unrelated copies.

## Configure and try it

Choose a writable notes file and allow Notifications if you want feedback. Enable the Rule, copy a harmless test phrase with surrounding spaces, and inspect the appended entry. Disable it when you do not want clipboard changes logged.

## Requirements and limits

Clipboard Changed, Transform Text, and Write to File require Rulr Pro. The Rule does not capture a page URL or citation. Clipboard contents can include private information, so use a suitable destination and disable the Rule when appropriate.
rules.intro:
Save copied text to a research notes file on Mac whenever the clipboard changes. Rulr trims the text, adds a timestamp, and appends it to the file.

The sample monitors clipboard changes continuously and writes to `~/Documents/Research Notes.txt`. Select a writable file and enable it only when you want this collection behavior.

rules.description: Reopen your usual browser workspace.
rules.documentation:
## Open a repeatable set of work pages

Use this Rule when the same two or more websites begin a work session. A single shortcut brings Chrome forward and opens the configured URLs, letting you start from a known set of destinations rather than finding bookmarks individually.

**When:** Press the chosen hotkey, initially Option + Space. **Do:** Activate Google Chrome and run two Open New Tab Actions. There is no If Condition. Both sample URLs are Google, so replace each one with a different work page if you want a useful workspace.

## Configure and try it

1. Import with **Open this Rule in Rulr** and choose a shortcut that does not conflict with your launcher or another Rule.
2. Edit each Open New Tab URL. Add or remove tab Actions to match the pages you need, keeping their order easy to understand.
3. Allow Accessibility access for application activation and Automation access for Google Chrome. Chrome must be installed on the Mac where you use the Rule.
4. Run the shortcut and verify that each configured address opens. Run it again deliberately to see how repeated invocations affect your tab list.

Keep this Rule when you want the same addresses on every run. If morning research and afternoon writing need different pages, start with [Chrome Research Workspace](/rules/chrome-research-workspace/) instead. The [AI Builder guide](/posts/build-mac-automations-with-ai/) shows how to request and review Conditions; check the [Chrome Actions](/capabilities/actions/#action.integration.chrome.open-new-window) before adding browser operations.

## Requirements and limits

The sample's components are available without Pro. Opening pages can still require network access and an existing login in Chrome; the Rule does not sign in to services for you.

Each run creates new tabs. It does not deduplicate existing tabs, restore a saved session, recover closed windows, or reproduce a previous layout. If you mainly need to find an already open page, use [Search Chrome Windows and Tabs](/rules/search-chrome-windows-tabs/).
rules.intro:
Start a work session on your Mac with one keyboard shortcut that activates Google Chrome and opens your configured work or research URLs in new tabs.

The Rule activates Google Chrome and opens each saved URL in a new tab. Choose the shortcut and tab URLs that make up your work or research workspace; this opens configured tabs rather than restoring a previous browser session.

Choose tab URLs

rules.documentation:
## How this Rule works

The hotkey runs the configured JavaScript in the current Chrome tab. Show Text or Image receives the result and displays it. There is no Condition and no automatic handling for other browsers.

## Configure and try it

Choose a shortcut, grant Accessibility and Automation access to Google Chrome, and review the JavaScript. Open a suitable Chrome tab, press the shortcut, and compare the displayed result with the page title. Chrome may require JavaScript from Apple Events to be enabled.

## Requirements and limits

rules.description: Keep new screenshots organized in an archive.
rules.documentation:
## Archive new screenshots by filename

This Rule is useful when screenshots arrive alongside other downloads and you want to move them into a separate review folder. It handles new items as they appear, so you can continue capturing references without manually moving each matching image.

**When:** A direct item is added to the watched folder. **If:** Its name matches the sample screenshot pattern. **Do:** Move the event's item path to the archive destination. The pattern looks for `screenshot` followed by a PNG or JPEG extension, ignoring letter case. It identifies names rather than inspecting image contents.

## Configure and try it

1. Use **Open this Rule in Rulr** to import the sample, then choose the folder where your screenshots actually arrive. The default watched path is Downloads.
2. Set Move File or Folder to a separate archive folder. The sample destination also points to Downloads, so choose your actual archive before enabling the Rule.
3. Review the filename Condition against one of your screenshots. Localized names or a different capture app may require a different pattern.
4. Enable the Rule and add a disposable matching image. Confirm that it moves and that a nonmatching image stays in place.

## Requirements and limits

Folder monitoring and moving files require Rulr Pro. Rulr also needs access to the source and destination folders. The numbered-name conflict option preserves separate names when a destination name is already taken.

The watcher covers direct children, not nested subfolders, and does not process an existing screenshot collection on import. To organize several file types, use [Sort Downloads](/rules/sort-downloads-mac/) instead.
rules.intro:
Move new Mac screenshots from a watched folder into an archive folder automatically, keeping the source folder easier to scan.

When a folder item is added, the Rule checks whether its name matches a screenshot file and moves the matching path to your archive. Choose the watched and archive folders before enabling it.
requiredConfiguration: Choose watched and archive folders

rules.description: Get warned when the battery reaches a low level.
rules.documentation:
## Add a spoken low-battery reminder

This Rule combines a visual notification with a spoken message when your Mac battery reaches a low level. It is useful when you work away from power and want an additional reminder that does not depend only on noticing the battery icon.

**When:** The battery level falls to or below 20%. **Do:** Show a notification and speak the configured text. There is no If Condition. The sample notification title and spoken message say `Low Battery Alert`; replace the generic notification content with instructions useful to you.

## Configure and try it

1. Import using **Open this Rule in Rulr** and review the threshold in Battery Level Changed. Choose a level that leaves enough time for your normal next step.
2. Edit the notification title, body, and sound setting. Review the Speak Text content separately so the spoken warning says what you intend.
3. Allow Notifications for Rulr and make sure your audio output and volume let you hear the speech.
4. Test the notification and speech Actions before relying on the battery event. To observe the full flow, use a suitable threshold and let the battery cross it while Rulr is running.

## Requirements and limits

Speak Text requires Rulr Pro. The Mac must expose battery-level information. System notification visibility also depends on macOS notification settings and whether Rulr is frontmost.

The Trigger represents a threshold crossing rather than a repeating alarm every minute while the battery remains low. The Rule does not plug in power, save documents, enable Low Power Mode, or shut the Mac down. For a separate routine when you step away, see [Mute and Close Private Apps When Idle](/rules/mute-close-apps-mac-idle/).
rules.intro:
Show a notification and speak a warning when your Mac battery falls to or below a configured threshold, so you can notice low power while working.

When the battery level reaches the configured threshold, the Rule shows a notification and speaks the warning aloud. Adjust the threshold and notification behavior to fit how you work away from power.
rules.title: Low Battery Alert

rules.description: Open your work tools on weekday mornings.
rules.documentation:
## Start a weekday workspace on a schedule

Use this Rule when your work session usually begins at a predictable time. It launches an application, opens a webpage, and posts a notification, providing a small scheduled starting routine that you can adapt to your own apps and destinations.

**When:** The weekly schedule reaches 09:00 on weekdays. **Do:** Launch Safari, open Google in Safari, and show the configured notification. There is no If Condition. The webpage and notification are included Actions in the sample; remove them explicitly if you only want an application launch.

## Configure and try it

1. Import through **Open this Rule in Rulr** and choose the days and time in the schedule Trigger. Review the displayed schedule on the Mac where it will run.
2. Select your application in Launch Application. Review the URL and application selected in Open URL separately; changing the launch app does not automatically change the browser Action.
3. Edit the notification text and sound, or remove the notification if it is unnecessary. Allow Notifications for Rulr if you retain it.
4. Set a temporary schedule a few minutes ahead while the Mac is awake and Rulr is running. Confirm the app, webpage, and notification, then restore your regular time.

## Requirements and limits

The sample's components are available without Pro. Selected apps must be installed, and the webpage may require network access or a login. System alerts also depend on macOS notification settings.

This routine does not wake a powered-off Mac, authenticate to work services, or restore a saved project. Keep Rulr available at the scheduled time and test your own sleep and wake routine. For manually starting an app group, see [Open Work Apps](/rules/open-work-apps-mac/).
rules.intro:
Launch selected Mac apps automatically at a scheduled weekday time, with an optional web page and notification for a repeatable morning setup.

The Rule runs on its weekly schedule, launches the configured application, opens the configured URL in Safari, and shows a notification. Choose the schedule, app, and URL before enabling it.
requiredConfiguration: Choose applications, URL, and schedule
rules.title: Morning Work Setup

rules.description: Open files when they are added to a watched folder.
rules.documentation:
## Open incoming files in their default app

Use this Rule for a small review inbox where each new document should open as soon as it arrives. It saves a trip to Finder when another workflow places a report or reference file in a folder you are actively watching.

**When:** A direct item is added to the selected folder. **If:** The event is an addition and the item kind is a file. **Do:** Open the Trigger's Item Path with its default application. The two Conditions keep folder additions from being opened by the sample.

## Configure and try it

1. Import using **Open this Rule in Rulr**, then choose the folder in Folder Contents Changed. The sample uses Downloads; a dedicated review folder is often easier to control.
2. Keep the change type set to added and review the file-kind Condition.
3. Review Open File or Folder. Its source should remain the event's Item Path, and its application choice should be Default unless you want a particular compatible app.
4. Enable the Rule and add a harmless text document. Confirm that the right app opens it. Add a folder separately and confirm that the Rule does not open it.

## Requirements and limits

Folder monitoring requires Rulr Pro. Rulr needs access to the watched folder, and macOS needs a suitable application for the file type.

The sample does not recursively monitor subfolders, open the existing contents on import, or wait for a browser's download-complete signal. Avoid using a busy general download folder until you have tested the behavior. For running your own processing steps instead of opening files, see [Run Shortcut for Folder](/rules/watch-folder-run-shortcut-mac/).
rules.intro:
Open each new file in its default application when it is added directly to a watched folder on your Mac, while leaving added folders unopened.

The Rule listens for an added folder item, checks that the changed item is a file, and opens its path with the default application. Choose a watched folder and test with a safe sample file before enabling it.
requiredConfiguration: Choose a watched folder

rules.description: Expand a short typed trigger into reusable text.
rules.documentation:
## Set up text expansion for repeated phrases

Use this Rule for a phrase you enter repeatedly, such as a reply, short address, or signature. A distinctive typed trigger starts an Insert Text Action so you can maintain the reusable content in one place rather than copying it from a reference note.

**When:** The exact phrase `;addr` is typed. **Do:** Insert the configured text into the frontmost application. There is no If Condition. The sample replacement content is `Text Expansion`; replace that demonstration value with your own phrase before using the Rule in real documents.

## Configure and try it

1. Import through **Open this Rule in Rulr** and review the Text Typed phrase and case-matching setting. Choose a trigger unlikely to appear in ordinary writing.
2. Edit Insert Text with your intended content. Begin with a short sentence so the result is easy to inspect.
3. Grant Accessibility access for the typed Trigger and text insertion. Enable the Rule and place the cursor in a temporary document in your usual writing app.
4. Type the trigger and check the full resulting text, including whether the trigger phrase remains and where the content is inserted. Repeat in other apps you intend to use.

## Requirements and limits

Text Typed requires Rulr Pro. The receiving app must support the simulated insertion behavior, and secure fields or app-specific input handling can behave differently.

The supplied flow contains a Trigger and insertion Action, without an explicit step to select or delete the typed abbreviation. Verify the result rather than assuming every app will replace it as a conventional snippet tool would.

## Is this a text replacement or snippet manager?

If you are migrating an AutoHotkey hotstring, read the [AutoHotkey for Mac alternatives guide](/posts/autohotkey-for-mac/) before choosing this Rule. It compares built-in Text Replacements with this insertion-only sample and other keyboard automation approaches.

This is one editable text expansion Rule, with one typed trigger and one configured insertion. It does not provide a searchable snippet library, synchronize snippets across devices, or guarantee that the trigger is removed. Use it when the event-to-insertion flow fits your app. For entering a new note each time instead of inserting a fixed phrase, use [Quick Note](/rules/quick-note-text-file-mac/).
rules.intro:
Set up a text expander Rule on Mac to insert reusable replies, addresses, or signatures when you type a short trigger. Choose your phrase and text in Rulr.

The sample matches `;addr` and inserts your configured text into the frontmost app. It has no explicit step to delete the typed abbreviation; check how it behaves in your writing app before relying on automatic replacement.
requiredConfiguration: Choose a typed trigger and replacement text
rules.title: Text Expansion

rules.description: Apply a consistent name to new watched files.
rules.documentation:
## Rename files automatically when they arrive in a folder

This Rule starts a naming workflow when an item appears in a folder. It is useful as a base for a controlled intake folder where incoming files need a recognizable name before you review or organize them elsewhere.

**When:** A direct item is added to the watched folder. **Do:** Pass its Item Path to Rename File or Folder. There is no filename or file-kind Condition in the sample. The configured replacement is the literal text `Processed File`, with numbered names used to resolve conflicts; it is not a date or project naming scheme.

## Configure and try it

1. Import through **Open this Rule in Rulr** and select a temporary intake folder for your first trial.
2. Review the replacement name and conflict handling in Rename File or Folder. Replace the sample text with the name you actually want; add supported Variables if you need a dynamic value.
3. Keep the source connected to the folder Trigger's Item Path so it refers to the arriving item.
4. Enable the Rule and add disposable files one at a time. Inspect their resulting names, extensions, and conflict behavior before using valuable documents.

## Requirements and limits

Folder monitoring and renaming require Rulr Pro and access to the watched folder. Because the sample has no file-kind filter, review how it should handle folder additions too. Add an explicit Condition if only a particular type should be renamed.

The Rule does not batch-rename the folder's existing contents or recursively watch subfolders. For moving files into different destinations rather than changing their names, use [Sort Downloads](/rules/sort-downloads-mac/).

## Can I batch rename files already in the folder?

This sample reacts to new additions rather than scanning the folder. It is intended for recurring file intake, not a one-time bulk rename of an existing selection. Start with an empty test folder and add disposable copies to confirm the replacement name and conflict behavior before using it for regular downloads.
rules.intro:
Automatically rename new files added to a folder on Mac. Choose the watched folder and replacement name, with numbered filenames to handle name conflicts.

Folder Contents Changed passes each new item's path to Rename File or Folder. The sample uses the literal name `Processed File`; replace it with your intended name before enabling the Rule.
requiredConfiguration: Choose a folder and naming pattern
rules.title: Rename New Files

rules.description: Open the right app when a USB device connects.
rules.documentation:
## Launch a Mac app when a USB device is connected

Use this Rule when connecting an accessory normally means opening the same utility or work app. The device-name Condition keeps the launch tied to the connection you care about.

**When:** A USB device connects. **If:** The event's Device Name contains `USB`. **Do:** Launch Safari. The sample performs a single app launch; it does not run an Apple Shortcut or pass device data into the app.

## Configure and try it

1. Import using **Open this Rule in Rulr** and replace `USB` with a distinctive part of the accessory's reported name.
2. Select the installed application you want to launch.
3. Enable the Rule, disconnect the accessory, and reconnect it. Check that the application opens.
4. Try a different USB device to confirm that the name Condition does not match too broadly. Adjust the filter if several accessories share the same name fragment.

## Requirements and limits

The sample's Trigger and Action are available without Pro and declare no special permission. The launched application may have its own device or permission requirements.

USB connection does not mean that a storage volume has mounted or that files are ready to read. This Rule does not import files, open a device-specific project, or identify accessories by serial number. For a routine implemented in Shortcuts, use [Run Shortcut for USB Device](/rules/run-shortcut-usb-device-mac/).

## Will every USB accessory open the app?

Only a connection whose reported name passes the Condition reaches the launch Action. Replace the sample `USB` substring with a selective name fragment. This name-based match can still match more than one device if they report similar names.
rules.intro:
Open an app automatically when a USB device connects to your Mac. Match your accessory's name and launch the utility or work app you use with it.

The sample matches names containing `USB` and launches Safari. Replace the broad name filter and select the app you use with your accessory after importing.
requiredConfiguration: Choose a USB device and application
rules.title: USB App Launcher

rules.description: Search the web using text selected in any supported Mac app.
rules.documentation:
## Search a selection without copying it manually

Use this Rule when a name, phrase, or unfamiliar term in a document needs a web search. It turns the current selection into a query and opens the results in Chrome, removing the manual copy, new-tab, and paste sequence.

**When:** Press the chosen shortcut, initially Option + Space. **Do:** Get Selected Text, URL-encode that text, and append the encoded result to Google's search URL before opening a new Chrome tab. There is no If Condition. The encoding step keeps spaces and punctuation from being interpreted as URL structure.

## Configure and try it

1. Import with **Open this Rule in Rulr** and assign an unused hotkey if Option + Space is already reserved.
2. Review the URL in Open New Tab. If you choose another search engine, retain the encoded-result Variable and use that service's query URL format.
3. Allow Accessibility and System Events Automation for selection retrieval, plus Google Chrome Automation for opening the tab.
4. Select a short phrase in a compatible app and run the Rule. Compare the query shown by the search engine with your selection, then repeat with punctuation or spaces.

## Requirements and limits

Transform Text requires Rulr Pro. Selected-text retrieval depends on the frontmost app exposing a usable selection; some apps may briefly use the clipboard during retrieval.

The selected phrase becomes part of a request to your configured search service. The Rule does not search local files, guarantee the first result, or replace text in the original document. For keeping the selection in a local notes file instead, use [Save Selected Text](/rules/save-selected-text-mac/).
rules.intro:
Select text in a Mac app and open a web search for it with one keyboard shortcut, without manually copying and pasting the query.

The Rule reads the current selection, URL-encodes it, and opens the search URL in Google Chrome. Change the URL template to use Google, DuckDuckGo, or another search service.
requiredConfiguration: Choose a shortcut and search provider
rules.title: Search Selected Text

rules.description: Quit a selected Mac app automatically at a scheduled time.
rules.documentation:
## Ask an app to quit at a chosen time

This Rule is useful for a repeatable end-of-session reminder expressed as an application action. It checks whether the selected app is running and requests a normal quit at the scheduled time, rather than requiring you to remember the same cleanup step each day.

**When:** The weekly schedule fires. **If:** Safari is running. **Do:** Quit Safari. The sample schedule is 09:00 on weekdays, so change it if you intend to close an app at the end of the day. The Condition and Quit Application Action must refer to the same intended application.

## Configure and try it

1. Import with **Open this Rule in Rulr** and select your days and time in the schedule Trigger.
2. Choose the target app in both the Running Applications Condition and Quit Application Action. Do not change only one of those fields.
3. Open the app with disposable work and set a temporary schedule a few minutes ahead while Rulr is running and the Mac is awake.
4. Observe the quit request, including any unsaved-document dialog. Test once with the app already closed to check the Condition, then restore the final schedule.

## Requirements and limits

The sample's components are available without Pro and declare no special permission. The app must be installed, and Rulr must be available to handle the schedule.

Normal quit can prompt for unsaved work or be delayed by an application. The Rule does not force termination, save every document, prevent relaunching, or enforce an app usage limit. For an inactivity-based routine instead of a fixed time, see [Mute and Close Apps When Idle](/rules/mute-close-apps-mac-idle/).

To close several apps together, [Quit Open Apps](/rules/quit-all-apps-mac/) uses a keyboard shortcut to list open apps and ask for confirmation before requesting normal quit. For an unresponsive frontmost app, [Recover a Stuck App](/rules/force-quit-shortcut-mac/) asks for confirmation before force quitting and reopening that app.
rules.intro:
Automatically quit a selected Mac application at a scheduled time, such as closing a work, communication, or entertainment app at the end of the day.

Choose the application and schedule after importing the Rule. The Rule checks that the app is running before asking it to quit normally.
requiredConfiguration: Choose an application and schedule
rules.title: Quit an App on a Schedule

rules.description: Run a Shortcut when watched folder contents change.
rules.documentation:
## Watch a Mac folder and trigger an Apple Shortcut

Use this Rule when an Apple Shortcut already performs your file-processing task and you want changes in a folder to start it. Rulr provides the event trigger, while the selected Shortcut remains responsible for what happens afterward.

**When:** A direct item is added to the watched folder. **Do:** Run an Apple Shortcut. The sample has no If Condition, no selected Shortcut, and a 30-second timeout. It does not automatically pass the changed item's path as input; configure an input connection if your Shortcut needs that information.

## Configure and try it

1. Import with **Open this Rule in Rulr**, then select the folder to watch. The sample uses Downloads and the added change type.
2. Choose an existing Shortcut in Run Shortcut. Run it manually in the Shortcuts app first so you know its setup and permissions are complete.
3. Review whether the Shortcut expects input and connect the relevant Trigger Variable if needed. Adjust the timeout for the actual task.
4. Enable the Rule and add a disposable file. Verify the Shortcut's expected result, then repeat with a second item to check that separate arrivals behave as intended.

When extending this workflow, review the [folder Trigger's parameters and outputs](/capabilities/#trigger.input.folder-contents-changed) separately from the Apple Shortcut's own settings. The [Mac automation guide](/posts/mac-automation/#can-i-combine-apple-shortcuts-and-applescript-in-one-workflow) explains combining existing Shortcuts with other Rule Actions.

## Requirements and limits

Folder monitoring requires Rulr Pro. Folder access and any permissions requested by the chosen Shortcut must be available on this Mac.

The watcher covers direct children, not nested contents, and an event is not a download-completion guarantee. Multiple arriving items can produce multiple runs, so choose a Shortcut suitable for repeated invocation. For opening each new file directly, use [Open New Files](/rules/open-new-files-mac/).

## Does the Shortcut receive the new file automatically?

The sample has no Shortcut input connected. If your Shortcut expects a file path, connect the folder Trigger's Item Path and confirm that the Shortcut accepts that value. The Rule starts the Shortcut; the Shortcut determines how the file is processed. For built-in routing without a separate Shortcut, use [Sort Downloads](/rules/sort-downloads-mac/).
rules.intro:
Run an Apple Shortcut automatically when a new file is added to a watched folder on Mac. Choose the folder and Shortcut to start your file-processing task.

The sample watches Downloads for added items and runs your chosen Shortcut with a 30-second timeout. Connect the event's Item Path as input if your Shortcut needs the arriving file.
requiredConfiguration: Choose a folder and Shortcut
rules.title: Run Shortcut for Folder

rules.description: Convert selected text to uppercase and replace it.
rules.documentation:
## Convert selected text to all caps with a Mac shortcut

Use this Rule when editing headings, labels, or short passages in an app that lacks a convenient uppercase command. The four Actions pass the text result forward, so the transformation applies to the selection you just made.

**When:** Press the configured hotkey, initially Option + Space. **Do:** Get Selected Text → Transform Text using uppercase → Set Clipboard → Paste Clipboard. There is no If Condition or app filter.

## Configure and try it

1. Import with **Open this Rule in Rulr** and choose an unused shortcut, especially if another imported Rule uses Option + Space.
2. Keep the uppercase transformation selected. Review the output references before changing the Action order.
3. Allow Accessibility and System Events Automation access for selection retrieval and pasting.
4. Select a short mixed-case phrase in an editable test document and run the shortcut. Check both the replacement and the clipboard before using it on important text.

## Requirements and limits

Transform Text requires Rulr Pro. Selection retrieval depends on the source app. The paste goes to the frontmost application's current insertion point or selection; keep focus on the intended field.

The Rule replaces the clipboard contents with the uppercase result and does not restore the previous clipboard. A read-only webpage cannot be edited by pasting. For whitespace cleanup of entered text instead, see [Trim Text](/rules/trim-copy-text-mac/).

## Does this turn on Caps Lock or change future typing?

It transforms the text you have already selected. It does not turn on Caps Lock, remap a key, or uppercase everything you type afterward. Keep the intended editable field frontmost until the clipboard paste finishes so the result reaches the correct selection.
rules.intro:
Convert selected text to uppercase on Mac with one keyboard shortcut. Rulr transforms the selection and pastes the all-caps result into your editable field.

The Rule gets the selection, transforms its case, puts the result on the clipboard, and pastes it. Choose a shortcut after importing and use it in an editable text field where pasting replaces the selection.
rules.title: Uppercase Selected Text

rules.description: URL-encode clipboard text and paste the result into the frontmost app with one keyboard shortcut.
rules.documentation:
## Paste clipboard text as a URL value

Use this Rule while preparing a query parameter or another URL value from text already on the clipboard. It converts that text with URL Encode, then inserts the transformed result at the current insertion point in your frontmost application.

**When:** Press Option + E. **Do:** Transform Current Clipboard Text using URL Encode, then Insert Text from the transformed Text Result. There is no If Condition. For example, a space in `hello world` becomes `%20`, producing `hello%20world` for a URL value.

## Configure and try it

1. Import with **Open this Rule in Rulr**. Review the shortcut, particularly if Option + E is used by your keyboard layout or another tool.
2. Keep Transform Text connected to Current Clipboard Text and set to URL Encode. Keep Insert Text connected to the transform's result rather than the original clipboard Variable.
3. Allow Accessibility permission for insertion and for recording a replacement shortcut if needed.
4. Copy a short phrase, place the cursor in a temporary text document, and run the Rule. Inspect the inserted output before trying it in the URL editor or form where you intend to use it.

## Requirements and limits

Transform Text requires Rulr Pro. The clipboard must contain text, and the receiving application must accept insertion at the current cursor position.

This sample is an encoding workflow. For pasting without the original styling, try the destination app's built-in Paste and Match Style command. This Rule does not decode a URL or decide whether an already encoded value should be encoded again. For trimming entered text instead of URL encoding, see [Trim Text](/rules/trim-copy-text-mac/).
rules.intro:
Press Option–E on your Mac to URL-encode clipboard text for a query parameter and insert the encoded result at the cursor in the frontmost app.

The Rule passes Current Clipboard Text through Transform Text with URL Encode, then sends the encoded output to Insert Text. Enable Accessibility permission for insertion and change the hotkey after import if Option–E is already in use.
requiredConfiguration: Choose a shortcut
rules.title: Paste URL-Encoded Text

rules.description: Switch Mac audio to a selected speaker or pair of headphones.
rules.documentation:
## Set a keyboard shortcut for your audio output device

To change the output once, open **System Settings → Sound → Output** and select the device. If the device is missing there, connect it and check the list again before assigning it in Rulr. See [Apple’s guide to sound output settings](https://support.apple.com/guide/mac-help/mchlp2256/mac).

Use this Rule when you often switch to the same speaker, headphones, or display audio device. A keyboard shortcut requests the selected output without opening Control Center and choosing the device manually each time.

**When:** Press the chosen hotkey, initially Option + Space. **Do:** Switch Audio Output Device. There is no If Condition. The sample has no device selected, so choosing an output is a required setup step after import rather than an optional customization.

## Configure and try it

1. Import with **Open this Rule in Rulr** and connect the audio device you want to use.
2. Select that device in Switch Audio Output Device. Review the choice on each Mac where you import the Rule, since available devices differ by machine and connection.
3. Assign an unused hotkey. Grant Accessibility access if you need to record a different combination.
4. Start quiet test audio, run the shortcut, and check the selected output in macOS Sound settings. Confirm that sound reaches the intended device. Disconnect it and review how the routine behaves when it is unavailable.

## Requirements and limits

The sample's Trigger and Action are available without Pro. The chosen device must be connected and available to macOS when the Action runs.

This Rule chooses one output device; it does not cycle through a device list, connect Bluetooth headphones, switch microphone input, or set a volume level. It also has no automatic fallback device configured. For applying volume after macOS changes output devices, see [Set Headphone Volume](/rules/set-volume-audio-device-mac/).

## Can I switch between headphones and speakers?

The imported sample selects one destination. For a separate keyboard shortcut to another output, create a second Rule, select the other connected device, and assign a different hotkey. Connect Bluetooth headphones before requesting them; changing the output is separate from pairing or connecting a device.

For play/pause control instead of choosing an output device, see the [Mac media playback control guide](/posts/mac-media-playback-control/). The [Mac automation guide](/posts/mac-automation/#mac-automation-examples) covers related audio and system Rules.
rules.intro:
Switch audio output on Mac with a keyboard shortcut. Send sound to your chosen headphones, speakers, or display without opening Sound settings each time.

Select one connected output device and choose the hotkey after importing. Each press requests that device; the sample does not cycle between devices or change the volume.
requiredConfiguration: Choose a shortcut and output device
rules.title: Switch Audio Output

rules.description: Copy the active Chrome tab URL to the clipboard.
rules.documentation:
## Copy the active tab's address

This Rule is useful when you want to share the page you are viewing without focusing Chrome's address bar and copying it manually. It retrieves the active tab URL and places that value on the clipboard for your next paste.

**When:** Press the configured shortcut, initially Option + Space. **Do:** Get Current Chrome Tab, then copy its Active Tab URL output. There is no If Condition. The Rule targets Google Chrome's active tab rather than a selected link, a Safari page, or every tab in the window.

## Configure and try it

1. Import with **Open this Rule in Rulr** and review Hotkey Pressed. Assign a distinct shortcut if another app or imported sample already uses Option + Space.
2. Allow Rulr to control Google Chrome when macOS requests Automation permission. Grant Accessibility access if you need to record a replacement shortcut.
3. Open an ordinary webpage in Chrome and select the tab you want to share. Run the Rule, then paste into a temporary note.
4. Compare the pasted address with Chrome's address bar. Switch to a second tab and repeat to verify that the Action reads the active tab at execution time.

The active tab's URL is an Action output, so keep the clipboard step connected to it when editing the Rule. The [Variables library](/capabilities/variables/) explains where component outputs are listed; the [Mac automation guide](/posts/mac-automation/#how-rulr-automates-your-mac) introduces passing results between steps.

## Requirements and limits

Get Current Chrome Tab requires Rulr Pro. Google Chrome must be installed with a tab available, and its Automation permission must be enabled for Rulr.

The result is only a URL: it does not include page text, a screenshot, or a title. Copying replaces the previous clipboard content and does not automatically send the link anywhere. For a title and URL formatted together, use [Copy Page as Markdown Link](/rules/copy-page-markdown-link-mac/).
rules.intro:
Copy the active Chrome tab's URL to your Mac clipboard with one keyboard shortcut, ready to paste into a message or note without selecting the address bar.

The Rule gets the active Chrome tab and sends its URL to the clipboard without changing tabs. Choose a shortcut and allow the required Chrome automation access.
rules.title: Copy Current Chrome URL

rules.description: Copy the current Chrome page title and URL as a Markdown link.
rules.documentation:
## Make a reference link for your notes

This Rule creates a Markdown reference from the current Chrome page, useful when collecting sources for documentation or a research note. It combines the document title and URL so you can paste a labeled link without writing the Markdown syntax yourself.

**When:** Press Option + M, or your replacement shortcut. **Do:** Run JavaScript in the active Chrome tab to format its title and URL, then place the script's result on the clipboard. There is no If Condition. The script escapes brackets and backslashes in the title and wraps the URL in angle brackets.

## Configure and try it

1. Import through **Open this Rule in Rulr** and review the hotkey. Accessibility access is needed if you record a different shortcut.
2. Allow Rulr to control Google Chrome through macOS Automation permission. Chrome must also permit JavaScript from Apple Events for the script Action to work.
3. Open an ordinary webpage in Chrome, run the Rule, and paste into a Markdown editor or a plain text note.
4. Check that both the label and destination describe the active page. Test a title containing punctuation and verify the link in your intended Markdown renderer.

For a research session that also opens your source pages, compare [Chrome Research Workspace](/rules/chrome-research-workspace/). Review the [Scripting Actions](/capabilities/actions/#actions-category-scripting) before changing the JavaScript, and use the [AI Builder review steps](/posts/build-mac-automations-with-ai/#3-review-it-on-the-visual-canvas) to inspect any proposed change to link formatting.

## Requirements and limits

Run JavaScript requires Rulr Pro. Some browser pages do not allow ordinary page scripts, so use a standard webpage for initial testing. Review Chrome's Apple Events JavaScript setting if Automation access alone does not resolve a script error.

The sample copies a link, without downloading the article or creating a full citation with author and publication date. It also replaces the prior clipboard text. For an unformatted address, see [Copy Current Chrome URL](/rules/copy-current-chrome-url-mac/).
rules.intro:
Copy the current Chrome page as a Markdown link containing its page title and URL, ready to paste into notes, documentation, or an issue tracker.

Press the chosen hotkey to read the active page title and URL in Chrome, format them as a Markdown link, and place the result on the clipboard.
requiredConfiguration: Choose a shortcut
rules.title: Copy Page as Markdown Link

rules.description: Sort new PDF downloads automatically.
rules.documentation:
## Give new PDFs a destination

Use this Rule when reports, invoices, or reference PDFs accumulate in Downloads and belong in one predictable folder. It moves a newly added matching item, keeping that document available in your chosen destination rather than requiring a separate Finder cleanup session.

**When:** A direct item is added to the watched folder. **If:** The item name ends in `.pdf`. **Do:** Move the path supplied by the folder event. The Condition checks the filename; it does not read the document or decide whether it is an invoice, report, or another kind of PDF.

## Configure and try it

1. Import with **Open this Rule in Rulr**, then choose the Downloads folder you want to monitor.
2. Choose a different PDF destination in Move File or Folder. Both sample paths initially point to Downloads, so the destination needs your attention before enabling the Rule.
3. Review the `.pdf` Condition and numbered-name conflict setting. Keep the event's Item Path Variable as the source so each run moves the new item.
4. Enable the Rule and add a disposable PDF. Check the destination, then add a non-PDF file to confirm it stays in the source folder.

## Requirements and limits

Folder monitoring and moving files require Rulr Pro and access to both folders. The watcher observes direct items, without recursively processing subfolders or moving PDFs that were already present before you enabled it.

A filename suffix does not validate a PDF's contents or prove a browser has finished writing it. Test your normal download workflow before relying on automatic moves. For separate image and archive destinations, see [Sort Downloads](/rules/sort-downloads-mac/).

{{< published-post-link path="/posts/hazel-alternative" label="Compare Rulr and Hazel for Mac file automation" >}}
rules.intro:
Automatically move new PDF downloads from a watched Downloads folder into a destination folder on your Mac.

When a new folder item is added, the Rule checks whether its name ends in `.pdf` and moves the matching path. Choose the watched Downloads folder and PDF destination before enabling it.
requiredConfiguration: Choose Downloads and PDF destination folders

A filename condition matches PNG, JPEG, GIF, HEIC and WebP extensions before Move File runs. The sample watches Downloads and also targets Downloads; choose a different destination first.

## Configure and try it

## Requirements and limits

rules.description: Run a selected Apple Shortcut when a matching USB device connects.
rules.documentation:
## Start a Shortcut when a USB device connects

Use this Rule for a device-specific setup routine, such as beginning a task when a USB accessory becomes available. It listens for the connection, filters the device's reported name, and starts an Apple Shortcut that you choose.

**When:** A USB device connects. **If:** Its Device Name contains `USB`. **Do:** Run Shortcut. The default filter is deliberately broad and the Shortcut is not selected, so both fields need review. The sample timeout is 30 seconds, and no device information is passed as Shortcut input by default.

## Configure and try it

1. Import with **Open this Rule in Rulr** and review the name Condition. Replace `USB` with a distinctive part of the device name you want to match.
2. Choose an existing Shortcut in Run Shortcut. Run it manually in the Shortcuts app first and complete any permissions or configuration it needs.
3. Review the timeout and any input required by your Shortcut. Connect an appropriate Trigger Variable if the task depends on device information.
4. Enable the Rule, disconnect the accessory, and reconnect it. Check the Shortcut's expected result, then try another device to verify the filter is selective enough.

## Requirements and limits

The sample's components are available without Pro and declare no special permission. The chosen Shortcut can have its own app, folder, or system requirements.

A USB connection is not the same as a mounted storage volume being ready. The Rule does not automatically copy files, identify every accessory uniquely, or wait for a drive mount. For starting processing from file arrivals instead, see [Run Shortcut for Folder](/rules/watch-folder-run-shortcut-mac/).
rules.intro:
Run an Apple Shortcut automatically when a matching USB device connects to your Mac, without opening the Shortcuts app first.

Choose the USB device match and Shortcut after importing the Rule. When that device connects, Rulr checks its name and runs the selected Shortcut.
requiredConfiguration: Choose a device and Shortcut

rules.description: Send new watched files through a shell script.
rules.documentation:
## How this Rule works

The folder Trigger passes the item path as the first script input. The supplied example prints that input and does not modify the file; select a folder and write your own script for additional processing.

## Configure and try it

Import the Rule, review its Trigger and Actions, and adjust the settings described above before enabling it. Test the result in a safe, temporary context.

## Requirements and limits

Folder monitoring and Run Shell Script require Pro. Review and test any replacement script on disposable files. The notification follows successful script execution, not independent verification of a file transformation.

rules.description: Download a selected link and reveal the saved file in Finder.
rules.documentation:
## Confirm a download from selected text

This Rule is a starting point for downloading a URL selected in another app. It reads text, applies the sample's filter, asks for confirmation, and reveals a successfully downloaded file in Finder so you can inspect the result.

**When:** Press Option + D. **Do:** Get Selected Text. **If:** That text contains `download`, continue to confirmation, Download from URL, and Reveal in Finder. The filter is a literal substring check, not a general URL validator. Many valid download addresses will not pass it until you change the Condition.

## Configure and try it

1. Import with **Open this Rule in Rulr** and review the shortcut and the `download` Condition. Replace the filter with criteria appropriate to your source links.
2. Select a destination folder; the sample uses Downloads. Review the 60-second download timeout and progress display.
3. Grant Accessibility and System Events Automation access for reading selected text. Use a compatible app where the selected content is the complete URL, not just a link's visible label.
4. Try a small public test file. First cancel the confirmation, then repeat and approve it. Check that only the successful run downloads and reveals a file.

## Requirements and limits

The confirmation and download Actions require Rulr Pro, plus access to the destination folder. The download is configured to stop the flow on failure, so Finder reveal depends on a successful file-path output.

This sample does not scrape a webpage for links or reproduce a browser's authenticated session. An incomplete selection, login page, or expired URL can fail. For organizing downloaded results afterward, see [Sort Downloads](/rules/sort-downloads-mac/).
rules.intro:
Download a selected link on your Mac with a keyboard shortcut, confirm the download, and reveal the finished file in Finder when it is ready.

Move File or Folder and Rename File or Folder can follow the download, allowing each result to enter a project folder, asset archive, or another file-organizing flow.
requiredConfiguration: Review the shortcut, link check, and download destination
rules.title: Download and Reveal a Link

rules.description: Prevent accidental shutdowns with confirmation.
rules.documentation:
## How this Rule works

When the shortcut is pressed, Show Confirmation displays a dialog. If it is cancelled, the Rule stops; otherwise Shut Down Computer runs. There is no Condition.

## Configure and try it

Choose an unused shortcut and change the dialog to clearly say it will shut down the Mac. Enable the Rule, press the shortcut, and test Cancel first. Save your work before testing confirmation.

## Requirements and limits

Show Confirmation requires Rulr Pro; the shortcut requires Accessibility. Confirming requests a real shutdown, and open apps or unsaved documents may affect the shutdown process.
rules.intro:
Use a keyboard shortcut to request shutdown on Mac with a confirmation dialog first. Cancelling the dialog stops the Rule before the shutdown Action.

The sample uses Option-Space and a generic confirmation message. Choose an unused shortcut and make the message explicit before enabling it.
requiredConfiguration: Choose a shortcut
rules.title: Confirm Before Shutdown

rules.description: See when the default microphone changes.
rules.documentation:
## Get notified when your Mac's default microphone changes

Use this Rule when connecting a headset or audio interface may change the Mac's default microphone. The notification gives you a visible cue to check the input before continuing a call or recording.

**When:** The audio input device changes. **Do:** Show a notification titled `Microphone Change Alert` with `Microphone changed to:` followed by the event's Device Name. Sound is enabled. There is no If Condition limiting notifications to a particular microphone.

## Configure and try it

1. Import with **Open this Rule in Rulr** and review the notification text. Preserve the Device Name Variable if you want to see which input was reported.
2. Choose whether the notification should play a sound, especially if you use the Rule while recording.
3. Allow Notifications for Rulr and enable the Rule.
4. Change the system's default audio input between two available devices and check the reported name. Repeat in the opposite direction to confirm both changes are visible.

## Requirements and limits

The sample's components are available without Pro. The Trigger declares no microphone recording permission; it observes the input-device change rather than recording audio. Notification visibility depends on macOS settings.

The Rule does not select a microphone, measure input levels, or change a meeting app's own input setting. An app that explicitly selects another microphone may differ from the system default. For output-device control, see [Switch Audio Output](/rules/switch-audio-output-mac/).

## Will this stop my Mac from switching microphones?

It reports the default input change; it does not prevent or reverse it. Use the reported device name as a prompt to review your system and meeting app input choices. The notification is triggered by a change, so it is not a continuously visible microphone status indicator.
rules.intro:
Get a Mac microphone change notification showing the new default input's name. Notice audio input switches while connecting a headset or recording equipment.

The Rule listens for Audio Input Device Changed and inserts the new device name into its notification. Customize the title, message, or sound after importing to suit your recording or meeting setup.
rules.title: Microphone Change Alert

rules.description: Switch your Mac to Dark appearance with a keyboard shortcut.
rules.documentation:
## Set macOS appearance to Dark

Use this Rule when you want a deliberate keyboard command for Dark appearance. It changes the system setting directly, which is useful before an evening work session or when you want to change appearance without navigating through System Settings.

Press Option + D to set macOS appearance to Dark from the app you are using.

**When:** Press Option + D, or your replacement shortcut. **Do:** Set System Appearance to Dark. There is no If Condition. The configured value is fixed: pressing the shortcut again keeps Dark appearance rather than toggling back to Light.

## What does a dark mode keyboard shortcut change?

This keyboard shortcut changes the Mac system appearance, not the color or backlight of a physical keyboard. To change appearance without a shortcut, open **System Settings → Appearance** and select **Dark**. The Rule is useful when you want to set Dark appearance from the keyboard while working in another app.

## Configure and try it

1. Import through **Open this Rule in Rulr** and review Hotkey Pressed. Choose another combination if Option + D is already assigned to a different app or Rule.
2. Review Set System Appearance and confirm that the selected value is Dark. Grant System Events Automation permission when macOS requests it.
3. Grant Accessibility if you need to record a replacement shortcut. Enable the Rule and start with macOS set to Light appearance for a visible first test.
4. Press the shortcut and check both System Settings and an app that follows the system theme. Press it again to confirm that it remains Dark. Restore your preferred appearance manually when finished testing.

## Requirements and limits

The sample's Trigger and Action are available without Pro. System Events Automation access is needed for the appearance change.

This changes the macOS appearance setting, not every application's independent theme preference. Apps with their own fixed Light or Dark setting may look unchanged. It also does not schedule sunset changes, dim the display, enable Night Shift, or create a two-way toggle. For a different keyboard-controlled utility routine, see [Toggle App Visibility](/rules/toggle-app-visibility-mac/).

To connect a hotkey to other system or application tasks, see the [Mac automation examples](/posts/mac-automation/#mac-automation-examples). That guide explains how Triggers and Actions fit together and links to separate Rules for audio output, apps, and files.
rules.intro:
Turn on Dark Mode on your Mac with a keyboard shortcut, changing the system appearance immediately without opening System Settings.

Launch Application Actions can follow Set System Appearance, extending the shortcut into an evening routine or an app workspace that opens in Dark appearance.
requiredConfiguration: Choose a shortcut
rules.title: Turn On Dark Mode with a Shortcut

## Requirements and limits
