rules.description: Paste clipboard text without source formatting into the frontmost app with Option + V.
rules.documentation:
For built-in shortcuts and app-specific fixes, start with the [guide to pasting without formatting on Mac](/posts/paste-without-formatting-mac/). This page demonstrates one importable Rulr Rule.

Rebuilding a Windows clipboard hotkey? The [AutoHotkey for Mac migration guide](/posts/autohotkey-for-mac/) shows how this Rule fits alongside app-launch and window-positioning shortcuts.

## A Rulr Rule for clipboard text without source formatting

When copying styled text into notes, email or a document, choose whether to keep the source formatting. This Rule adds a separate plain-text paste shortcut alongside normal paste:

- **Command + V (⌘V):** Paste normally using the destination app's existing command.
- **Option + V (⌥V):** Convert the current clipboard text to plain text and insert it at the cursor in the frontmost app.

Copy formatted text from a webpage or document, focus an editable field in the app you want to paste into, and press Option + V. No destination app is fixed in the Rule; keep your destination focused until insertion finishes.

**When:** Press Option + V. **If:** No Condition; the Rule runs whenever its shortcut is pressed while enabled. **Do:** Convert Current Clipboard Content to plain text, then insert the Plain Text output.

The second Action uses the first Action's output. Insert Text sends the converted text as keyboard input to the focused app; the destination field must accept that input. It does not invoke the app's Paste and Match Style command.

## Configure and try it

1. Import the Rule using **Open this Rule in Rulr**. Choose another shortcut if Option + V conflicts with your keyboard layout or another app.
2. Confirm Convert to Plain Text uses Current Clipboard Content and Insert Text uses the conversion's Plain Text output.
3. Allow Accessibility access, enable the Rule, and copy a formatted passage from a webpage or document.
4. Place the cursor in a temporary editable document and press the shortcut. Compare the inserted words with the original and check that the source styling has been removed. The destination can still apply its own font, size, or color.

## If the shortcut does not insert text

- Confirm the Rule is enabled and Rulr has Accessibility access.
- Check that Option + V is not assigned to another action or needed by your keyboard layout; choose another shortcut if necessary.
- Focus an editable field before pressing the shortcut.
- Copy a single text item. Clipboard content with image or file data, or multiple clipboard items, is not supported by this conversion.

## Requirements and limits

The Rule requires a version of Rulr that includes Convert to Plain Text and Accessibility access for insertion. It accepts one clipboard item containing supported plain text, RTF, or HTML. Content with image or file data is rejected even if a text representation is also present; multiple clipboard items are not supported. It does not extract text from images or read the contents of copied files.

Conversion removes source styling. It does not correct grammar, trim spaces, or join line breaks from copied PDFs. The destination controls the appearance of the inserted text, so plain text can still take on the surrounding paragraph's formatting.

The sample converts and immediately inserts text when you press its shortcut. It does not remap Command + V or make every paste plain text automatically. To extend the Rule, use the Plain Text output as input to another Action.

Check insertion in the apps and fields you plan to use. Sending keyboard input does not confirm that the destination accepted it.

For Paste and Match Style, Word and Google Docs shortcuts, or a TextEdit fallback, see [Paste without formatting on Mac: shortcuts and fixes](/posts/paste-without-formatting-mac/).

For a copied URL, use [Open Clipboard Link](/rules/open-clipboard-link-mac/) to review it before opening Safari. Neither Rule stores clipboard history.
rules.intro:
This Rulr Rule demo uses Option + V on Mac to convert the current clipboard item to plain text and insert it into the frontmost app. Import and enable the Rule to use this separate shortcut alongside normal Command + V paste.

The sample uses Option + V to run Convert to Plain Text on Current Clipboard Content, then passes its Plain Text output to Insert Text. Choose another shortcut if needed.
requiredConfiguration: Allow Accessibility access; change Option + V if needed
rules.title: Paste as Plain Text

rules.description: Preview or add a prefix to matching files in a folder on a schedule.
rules.documentation:
## How this Rule works

- **When:** Timed Repeat runs every 30 minutes, between 00:00 and 24:00 by default.
- **If:** There is no Condition node. The script filters matching files and checks destination conflicts before renaming.
- **Do:** Run Shell Script invokes the embedded Bash script. It previews the names by default; setting its mode to `apply` adds the prefix to matching filenames.

For example, `invoice.pdf` becomes `project-invoice.pdf`. Files already beginning with the same prefix are skipped, including files that had that prefix before the first run. New matching files can be handled on later runs.

The imported Rule is disabled. Its folder setting is empty, so it will report an error until you set an existing absolute folder path. It does not download code or install a script when it runs.

## Configure and try it

1. Add the Rule to Rulr and leave it disabled while configuring it.
2. Open **Do → Run Shell Script → Script**. Keep **text script** mode and edit only the four settings at the top initially:

```bash
folder="/absolute/path/to/Rename Demo"
mode="preview"
extension="pdf"
prefix="project-"
```

3. Choose a disposable folder containing copies of a few PDFs. Enter its absolute path inside the quotes; do not use `~`. For paths containing a literal dollar sign, backtick, backslash, or quote, use appropriate shell quoting rather than pasting them unchanged into double quotes.
4. Keep `preview` while testing. The extension has no leading dot and is case sensitive. The prefix accepts letters, digits, hyphens, and underscores.
5. Review **When → Timed Repeat**. You can temporarily shorten the interval to one minute. Leave the optional script Argument empty, the timeout at 30 seconds, and **Stop this flow if unsuccessful** enabled.
6. Enable the Rule and enter Inspect Mode. Wait for a timer run, confirm success, and check that preview has left filenames unchanged. Disable the Rule before editing again.
7. Review the complete preview in Terminal using the download below if needed. When satisfied, change `mode="preview"` to `mode="apply"`, enable the Rule for a test, and verify the filenames and contents on disk.
8. Disable the Rule after testing. Before recurring use, select the intended folder, keep a backup, and choose an interval longer than the expected runtime.

The rest of the embedded script implements matching, conflict checks, and moves. You do not need to replace it or install a separate file to use this Rule. Changes to your embedded copy are local; downloading a newer website script does not update an imported Rule automatically.

## Download the standalone script

[Download batch-prefix-files.sh](/scripts/batch-prefix-files.sh) to use the same renaming logic in Terminal. Read it and save it locally before running. For example, after replacing these paths:

```bash
/bin/bash "/absolute/path/to/batch-prefix-files.sh" preview "/absolute/path/to/Rename Demo" pdf project-
```

Use `apply` only after reviewing the preview. The downloadable script is the source embedded by the Gallery generator, so the Rule and download share the same renaming logic.

For Finder's built-in rename options and a complete command walkthrough, see [how to batch rename files on Mac](/posts/mac-batch-rename-files/).

## Requirements and limits

Run Shell Script requires **Rulr Pro**, and Rulr requires macOS 26 or later. Rulr must have access to the selected folder; a successful Terminal run does not prove the app has the same access. The text script explicitly invokes `/bin/bash` because the Action's outer interpreter is `/bin/sh`.

Only ordinary, non-hidden files in the folder's first level are processed. Subfolders and symbolic links are skipped. Passing `pdf` leaves `.PDF` unchanged. The script preserves the rest of the name and file contents; it does not number files, replace text, or read a Finder selection.

Apply checks all planned destinations before starting and refuses existing files, directories, or symbolic links. A directory lock coordinates other instances of this script. Keep the folder unchanged during a batch: Finder and other programs do not honor that lock. Interrupted runs or external changes can leave a partially completed batch; there is no automatic rollback. A forced termination may leave a lock requiring review before another run.

Rulr captures at most 1,024 bytes of script output, and Execution Logs redact script text. Use Terminal for a complete preview of a large folder, and verify actual files rather than treating an Action's success as a complete rename history.

For individual new arrivals instead of existing folder contents, use [Rename New Files](/rules/rename-new-files-mac/). Explore more tasks in [Mac file automation](/rules/files-organization/).
rules.intro:
Batch rename matching files in a Mac folder by adding a prefix on a schedule. This Rulr Rule starts with a preview so you can review the proposed names before applying changes.

Set the folder path in the included script, choose an extension and prefix, then review the timer. The script is embedded in the Rule; a separate download is available below for Terminal use.
requiredConfiguration: Set the folder path in the embedded script and review preview before choosing apply
Review the interval, extension, prefix, folder access, and Pro requirement
rules.title: Batch Prefix Files

rules.description: Confirm, force quit and reopen the frontmost app when it stops responding.
rules.documentation:
## Recover the app that stopped responding

**When:** Press Option + 1 while the affected app is frontmost. **Do:** Run AppleScript to capture that app, show its name and ask for confirmation. On approval, it force terminates that process, waits up to five seconds for termination and reopens the captured bundle identifier.

This is a recovery sequence, rather than another way to open the system Force Quit chooser. It handles reopening so you do not have to find the app again afterward.

## Configure and try it

1. Import the Rule and review the shortcut and recovery script.
2. Save work before trying it. Focus a disposable app such as a test TextEdit session.
3. Enable the Rule, press Option + 1 and check the application name in the dialog.
4. Choose **Cancel** first; the target should stay open.
5. For an intentional recovery attempt, choose **Force Quit and Reopen**. Verify that the named application closes and reopens.

## Requirements and limits

Run AppleScript does not require Pro. This Rule uses AppKit because Rulr's normal Quit Application Action does not provide force termination or dynamic relaunch.

Force quit can lose unsaved changes. Reopening does not guarantee restored documents, tabs or work. If termination is not observed, the script stops without reopening. Finder, Rulr and Script Editor are excluded.

If the whole Mac or Rulr is unresponsive, use the system recovery controls. For normal cleanup, use [Quit Open Apps](/rules/quit-all-apps-mac/).
rules.intro:
Recover a stuck Mac app with Option + 1: confirm its name, force quit that specific application and reopen it automatically.

The Rule snapshots the frontmost application before showing a confirmation. It keeps Finder, Rulr and Script Editor out of the recovery path and never force quits without confirmation.
requiredConfiguration: Review Option + 1 and enable the imported Rule
Focus the stuck app and review the force-quit warning; unsaved work can be lost
rules.title: Recover a Stuck App

rules.description: Move newly created video-app windows to your presentation display and toggle full screen.
rules.documentation:
## Open the video on your presentation screen

**When:** A window is created by QuickTime Player. **Do:** Move Window to Screen moves that event's window to your chosen display, then Toggle Full Screen requests a full-screen transition. There is no script.

Use this when opening a video for a projector or second monitor. The system full-screen keyboard shortcut changes a focused window manually; this Rule reacts to the selected application's new windows.

## Configure and try it

1. Import the Rule and choose the video app in Window Created.
2. Select the actual presentation monitor in Move Window to Screen.
3. Keep both window targets connected to the Window Created output.
4. Allow Accessibility, enable the Rule and open a disposable video in a new normal window.
5. Confirm that this window moves to the chosen monitor and enters full screen. Create another window while a different app is focused to check the target.

## Requirements and limits

Window Created and Move Window to Screen require Pro; Toggle Full Screen does not. Allow Accessibility.

Every window-creation event reported for the chosen app can trigger the Rule, including non-document windows the app exposes. A missing display or unsupported window can stop the flow.

The move step rejects windows already in full screen, and the final Action toggles state rather than setting an unconditional on state. Avoid combining this Rule with another app feature that automatically makes the same window full screen.

For a manual layout on the current Desktop, see [Move Window to Left Half](/rules/snap-window-left-mac/).
rules.intro:
Automatically move new QuickTime Player windows to your presentation display on Mac, then request full screen. Open the video normally; there is no extra Rule shortcut to press.

Choose the video application in Window Created and your monitor in Move Window to Screen. Both Actions target the window supplied by the creation event, rather than whichever app later becomes focused.
requiredConfiguration: Review the event Trigger and required setup before enabling
Choose the video application and presentation display; QuickTime Player is the sample app
rules.title: Present New Video Windows

rules.description: Put selected Finder items into a new folder whose name you choose.
rules.documentation:
## Put a Finder selection into a named folder

**When:** Press Option + 3. **If:** Finder is frontmost. **Do:** Run AppleScript to snapshot the selection, check that the items share a parent, ask for a name, create that folder and move the selected items into it.

Use it to collect the files for a handoff or project without creating a folder, renaming it and dragging the selection separately. The built-in Control-Command-N also groups a Finder selection; this Rule supplies an explicit name prompt and checks its destination before moving.

## Configure and try it

1. In a disposable folder, select two or three test files.
2. Import the Rule, review the shortcut and allow Finder Automation when requested.
3. Enable it, focus Finder and press Option + 3.
4. Enter a new folder name and choose **Create and Move**.
5. Confirm that the selected items moved into the new folder and unselected items stayed put. Try Cancel and an existing name separately.

## Requirements and limits

Run AppleScript does not require Pro. The script handles Finder's live selection because the current native file Actions do not expose a selected-file collection.

This moves existing items, rather than copying or backing them up. An empty selection or items from different parent folders are rejected. Permissions or a failed move can leave a partially completed operation; inspect the folders before retrying.

The folder stays inside the original parent. It is not moved one directory upward.

For incoming files instead of a selection, see [Mac file automation](/rules/files-organization/).
rules.intro:
Group selected Finder files into a new named folder on Mac with Option + 3. The Rule asks for the folder name and moves the captured selection into it.

Select items in one Finder folder first. The Rule keeps the new folder beside those items, rejects an existing destination name and reveals the resulting folder.
requiredConfiguration: Review Option + 3 and enable the imported Rule
Select items in one Finder folder, allow Finder Automation and choose a new folder name
rules.title: Group Selected Files

rules.description: Replace the clipboard with an innocuous marker after five minutes of system inactivity.
rules.documentation:
## Replace copied content when you step away

**When:** System Idle reaches five minutes. **Do:** Set Clipboard to Text replaces the current item with EMPTY. There is no script, shortcut or confirmation.

Use it as a cleanup step for content that should not remain ready for accidental pasting after a break. It replaces any current copied item, including an image or file reference.

## Configure and try it

1. Import the Rule and review the five-minute idle threshold and EMPTY marker.
2. Temporarily choose a shorter interval for a deliberate trial.
3. Enable the Rule, copy a disposable phrase and stop using the mouse and keyboard until the threshold is reached.
4. Resume and paste into a blank document. Confirm that EMPTY is pasted instead of the old phrase.
5. Restore the intended idle threshold.

## Requirements and limits

The Trigger and Set Clipboard to Text do not require Pro or declare special permissions.

System inactivity is not the time since copying, app inactivity or screen lock. A later copy does not start a dedicated clipboard timer; the Trigger follows system user-input activity. Sleeping or shutting down the Mac is not a guaranteed cleanup opportunity.

The marker replaces the current content rather than producing a zero-byte pasteboard. It does not securely erase previous copies, other devices or third-party clipboard-manager history. The prior clipboard item cannot be recovered through this Rule.

For cleaning the content of newly copied text instead, see [Remove Emoji from Text](/rules/remove-emojis-from-text-mac/).
rules.intro:
Clear old copied content from the current Mac clipboard after five minutes of system inactivity. The Rule replaces it with the harmless text EMPTY when you step away.

Choose the idle threshold after importing. This reacts to time without user input, rather than requiring you to remember a cleanup shortcut.
requiredConfiguration: Review the event Trigger and required setup before enabling
Review the five-minute system-idle threshold and EMPTY marker before enabling
rules.title: Clear Clipboard When Away

rules.description: Automatically remove common emoji sequences when matching text is copied.
rules.documentation:
## Clean copied text before the next paste

**When:** Clipboard Changed fires. **If:** That event's Text matches the emoji-sequence expression. **Do:** Replace Text removes matching sequences from the event's text, then Set Clipboard to Text copies the result.

This is useful when gathering text for a plain report or data field that should omit emoji. Copy as usual; the Rule does not need a separate cleanup shortcut.

## Configure and try it

1. Import the Rule and review the matching Condition and replacement pattern.
2. Enable it and copy a disposable passage containing ordinary words, non-Latin characters and emoji.
3. Wait for execution, then paste into a separate blank document.
4. Confirm that the intended emoji are removed and the remaining text is preserved.
5. Copy ordinary text without emoji and confirm that the Condition skips it.
6. Disable the Rule when you want to preserve copied emoji.

## Requirements and limits

Clipboard Changed and Replace Text require Pro. This Rule does not read the current document selection or edit the source document.

Writing the cleaned result generates another clipboard event. The same Condition rejects that result when no matched emoji remain, so it does not repeatedly clean its own output.

The pattern targets common pictographs, joined sequences, modifiers, flag pairs and keycaps. Unicode support depends on macOS; unusual or new sequences may remain, and text-style pictographs may match.

Matching copies become plain text and lose source formatting. Cleanup runs asynchronously; pasting before it finishes can use the original content, and rapid consecutive copies need care.

For report-number extraction from copied text, see [Extract Line-End Number](/rules/remove-line-breaks-regex-mac/).
rules.intro:
Automatically remove common emojis when you copy text on Mac. The Rule checks the clipboard-change event for matching sequences, then replaces the copied text with the cleaned result.

Enable this only when you want matching copies cleaned automatically. The Condition prevents ordinary text and the already-cleaned result from entering the replacement flow.
requiredConfiguration: Review the event Trigger and required setup before enabling
Requires Pro; enabling automatically cleans matching copied text; review the matching Condition
rules.title: Remove Emoji from Text

rules.description: Run your configured AppleScript file on a weekday schedule.
rules.documentation:
## Automate a script you already maintain

**When:** The configured weekday schedule fires. **Do:** Run AppleScript loads your configured file from disk and runs it. The file is read on each execution, so later changes to that file do not need to be pasted back into the Rule.

A report, calendar or maintenance script can run without opening Script Editor each time. The Rule supplies scheduling and file loading; your script supplies the actual work.

## Configure and try it

1. Choose a trusted .scpt or .applescript file that you already understand and have run manually.
2. In Run AppleScript, add a text Argument containing its absolute path or a path beginning with ~/.
3. Review the embedded loader and set the days and time in the Trigger.
4. Start with a harmless script and a temporary near-future schedule while the Mac is awake.
5. Enable the Rule, inspect its execution and verify the chosen script's expected result before restoring the intended schedule.

## Requirements and limits

Run AppleScript does not require Pro. The loader stops with a configuration error if no file path Argument is present. This imported sample needs your actual file path before it can run.

The file can request Automation or folder access. Only load scripts you trust. The loader supplies no arguments to your saved script and has a 120-second timeout. It does not wake a sleeping Mac or guarantee compiled-script compatibility across macOS versions.

The direct Rulr script-file picker and this compiled-file loader have different format support. For entered text processing, see [Process Text with AppleScript](/rules/process-text-applescript-mac/).
rules.intro:
Run a saved .scpt AppleScript file on a Mac schedule, such as a report-preparation script that reads Numbers and creates Calendar events.

Configure the trusted file path in the Run AppleScript Action's Arguments, then choose your schedule. The sample is disabled and scheduled for weekdays at 09:00; it includes no report-processing script of its own.
requiredConfiguration: Review the event Trigger and required setup before enabling
Set the trusted script path in Arguments and review the weekday 09:00 schedule before enabling
rules.title: Schedule AppleScript File

rules.description: Close other Finder windows while leaving the current one open.
rules.documentation:
## Keep the folder you are working in

**When:** Press Option + 7. **If:** Finder is frontmost. **Do:** Run AppleScript to capture the Finder windows behind its front window, then close those other windows.

This is useful after browsing many folders: keep the current working location and clear the clutter. It differs from Option-Command-W, which closes the current window along with the others.

## Configure and try it

1. Open three ordinary Finder windows in disposable folders.
2. Bring the one you want to keep to the front.
3. Import the Rule, review Option + 7 and allow Finder Automation.
4. Enable it and press the shortcut with Finder still frontmost.
5. Confirm that the front window remains and the other windows close. Try again with one window; nothing else should close.

## Requirements and limits

Run AppleScript does not require Pro. The Rule needs Finder Automation access. Rulr's native All Windows target cannot express “all except the front window,” which is why this adapted workflow uses a small Finder script.

The script targets Finder's window order, including windows reported on other Spaces. It closes tabs contained in the other windows but keeps the retained window's tabs. It does not delete files, quit Finder or restore closed browsing state.

For a named folder from the current selection, use [Group Selected Files](/rules/new-folder-hotkey-mac/).
rules.intro:
Clear other Finder windows on Mac with Option + 7 while keeping the window you are using. The Rule closes Finder windows behind that front window.

Bring the Finder window you want to keep to the front first. The script snapshots windows with an index greater than one and closes those windows, leaving the front window and its tabs open.
requiredConfiguration: Review Option + 7 and enable the imported Rule
Bring the Finder window to keep to the front and allow Finder Automation
rules.title: Keep Current Finder Window

rules.description: Use a keyboard shortcut to review and quit open apps together, keeping Finder and Rulr open.
rules.documentation:
## How to quit all open apps on Mac together

At the end of a work session, save your documents and use one shortcut to review the apps you want to close. You do not need to quit a particular application first.

**When:** Press Option + 8. **Do:** Run AppleScript takes a snapshot of regular GUI apps and presents their names. Choosing **Quit Apps** requests normal termination for the listed apps. Cancel is the default choice.

Finder, Rulr and Script Editor stay open. The batch covers eligible open apps, rather than every process on the Mac, and each app can show its own save dialog.

## Configure and try it

1. Import the disabled Rule and review Option + 8. Choose an unused combination if needed.
2. Review the script's excluded application bundle identifiers and save your work before trying the flow.
3. Allow Accessibility access for the hotkey and enable the Rule.
4. Press the shortcut, review the app list and choose **Cancel** first; those apps should stay open.
5. For a deliberate trial, open disposable apps without unsaved work, press the shortcut again and confirm.
6. Answer any save dialogs and check which apps remain. An app that declines or delays quitting can stay open.

To run this at a session boundary instead, replace Hotkey Pressed with Application Quits and choose your main work app. Any reported quit of that app, including an unexpected exit, can then trigger the confirmation. The downloadable sample uses the manual shortcut.

## Requirements and limits

Hotkey Pressed and Run AppleScript do not require Pro. Accessibility access is needed for the shortcut. No apps are force killed.

The app list is captured before confirmation. Check it before approving: it includes regular GUI apps rather than an inferred project membership.

Finder, Rulr and Script Editor are excluded. Menu-bar-only utilities, background agents and apps launched after the snapshot are not included. An accepted quit request does not guarantee completed termination; apps can display save dialogs or decline.

For a stuck app that needs force termination and reopening, use [Recover a Stuck App](/rules/force-quit-shortcut-mac/). To close selected companion tools after a particular app exits, see [Close Work Apps](/rules/quit-companion-apps-mac/).
rules.intro:
Quit open apps together on Mac with a keyboard shortcut and a confirmation. Option + 8 lists eligible apps and requests normal quit after you approve, keeping Finder, Rulr and Script Editor open.

Change Hotkey Pressed to an unused combination and review the script's exclusions. Apps can ask you to save documents or decline to quit; the Rule does not force termination.
requiredConfiguration: Review Option + 8 and enable the imported Rule
Review Option + 8 and the app exclusions; save work and check the app list before confirming
rules.title: Quit Open Apps

rules.description: Capture a region, ask for a filename and save the named PNG in your chosen folder.
rules.documentation:
## Name the screenshot while its purpose is fresh

**When:** Press Option + 9. **Do:** Capture Screen or Window lets you select an area at execution time. Ask for Input collects the filename, Rename appends .png, Move saves it into the configured destination, and Reveal shows the saved image.

This suits bug reports, receipts or research captures that need a meaningful name. It avoids hunting for a newly created screenshot and renaming it afterward.

## Configure and try it

1. Import the Rule and choose the destination in Move File or Folder.
2. Allow Screen Recording and folder access, review the shortcut and enable it.
3. Press Option + 9 and select a harmless screen region.
4. Enter a filename without .png, then confirm.
5. Inspect the named PNG in the destination. Try an existing name to confirm that the Rule stops instead of replacing it.

## Requirements and limits

Rename and Move require Pro; capture, input and reveal do not. The default target is Capture on Run. You can select a different supported capture target in the Action.

This adaptation uses one configured capture mode and stops on a duplicate name. It does not include a loop that repeatedly asks for a different name. Cancelling the name prompt leaves the captured image in its temporary location.

A failed capture, rename or move stops the flow. The Rule does not perform OCR or redact content. For recognized text, use [Copy Text from Your Screen](/rules/copy-text-mac-screen/).
rules.intro:
Capture a Mac screen region, name it and save it to your chosen folder with Option + 9. The Rule asks for the filename immediately after capture.

Choose the destination in Move File or Folder after importing; it initially uses Downloads. The flow uses native capture, input, rename, move and reveal Actions, without watching a screenshots folder.
requiredConfiguration: Review Option + 9 and enable the imported Rule
Requires Pro; choose a destination, capture a region, then enter a filename without .png
rules.title: Capture and Name Screenshot

rules.description: Show a line-end number automatically when matching report text is copied.
rules.documentation:
## Read a reference number while copying a report

**When:** Clipboard Changed fires. **If:** The event's Text contains slash-digits followed by a line break or the end of text. **Do:** Extract Text returns the first matching number, and Show Text or Image displays it.

The Condition and extraction use this newline-aware expression:

```text
/(\d+)(?=\R|$)
```

For example, copying a report line ending in reference/123 shows 123 without an extra extraction shortcut. Capture group 1 omits the slash and newline.

## Configure and try it

1. Import the Rule and review both copies of the pattern, the first-match setting and capture group 1.
2. Enable it and copy a disposable line ending in reference/123.
3. Confirm that the result panel shows 123.
4. Try the same line with a trailing newline and then without one.
5. Copy ordinary text with no match; the Condition should skip the extraction.
6. Adjust both patterns together for your actual report format.

## Requirements and limits

Clipboard Changed and Extract Text require Pro. The Rule does not modify the clipboard, remove line breaks or edit the source document.

Only the first matching number is displayed. A space after the digits prevents this pattern from matching that line ending. A newline previously removed by another tool cannot be detected; the end-of-text alternative covers a final number without a newline.

Every matching clipboard-change event can show a panel, so enable this only when useful for the reports you are processing. For automatic content cleanup, compare [Remove Emoji from Text](/rules/remove-emojis-from-text-mac/).
rules.intro:
Automatically show a report number when you copy text containing slash-digits at a line ending on Mac. The Rule checks the clipboard-change event before extracting the first matching number.

Extract Text reads the event's text and returns capture group 1. Ordinary copied text is skipped, and the Rule leaves the clipboard unchanged.
requiredConfiguration: Review the event Trigger and required setup before enabling
Requires Pro; a result is shown only for copied text with slash-digits at a line ending
rules.title: Extract Line-End Number

rules.description: Convert English letters to alphabet positions, or positions back to letters.
rules.documentation:
## Use letters as numbers in an alphabet exercise

**When:** Press Option + L. **Do:** Ask for Input collects English letters or space-separated positions, Run AppleScript converts them, then Show Text or Image displays the result.

Use it for alphabet-position exercises or preparing a value to use in a spreadsheet. Unlike a shortcut remap, the Rule performs the conversion itself.

## Configure and try it

1. Import the Rule, review Option + L and choose an unused shortcut if needed.
2. Enable it and enter HELLO. Check that the panel displays 8 5 12 12 15.
3. Run it again and enter 8 5 12 12 15. Check that it displays HELLO.
4. Try a single letter or position, then cancel the input prompt to stop the flow.
5. Review any input error instead of treating it as a conversion result.

## Requirements and limits

Ask for Input, Run AppleScript and Show Text or Image do not require Pro. The hotkey Trigger requires Accessibility access. The conversion has no external dependency and does not automate a spreadsheet application.

Letters must be English A–Z; letter case is ignored and spaces are skipped. Numeric input must use integer positions from 1 to 26 separated by spaces. The script rejects decimals, punctuation and out-of-range positions, and limits each input to 200 characters to keep the displayed result bounded.

This is an alphabet-position conversion. AA becomes 1 1, not spreadsheet column 27. It does not turn a numeric string into a word's meaning, use another writing system or edit workbook cells.

The result is displayed without replacing the clipboard. For a different text transformation, see [Process Text with AppleScript](/rules/process-text-applescript-mac/).

For the separate Apple News word puzzle, see [Find Quartiles Word Candidates](/rules/quartiles-word-candidates-mac/).
rules.intro:
Convert letters to numbers on Mac with A1Z26, where A=1 through Z=26, or convert a list of positions back to letters. Enter HELLO to get 8 5 12 12 15, or enter those positions to get HELLO.

The Rule asks for input, passes it to an embedded AppleScript and shows the result. It does not read or modify a Numbers or Excel workbook.
requiredConfiguration: Review Option + L and the A=1 through Z=26 conversion; no external dependency
rules.title: Letters and Alphabet Positions

rules.description: Advance a chosen Safari article by one screen every 30 seconds while reading.
rules.documentation:
## Repeat Space for a reading task

Read a long Safari article while taking notes on paper or sitting away from the keyboard. This Rule presses Space at a fixed interval to move down the article one screen at a time.

Safari uses Space to move down one screen, as documented in [Apple's Safari keyboard shortcuts](https://support.apple.com/guide/safari/keyboard-shortcuts-and-gestures-cpsh003/mac). The timer performs that repeated operation for you; it does not replace a single shortcut with another shortcut.

**When:** Every 30 seconds. **If:** Safari is frontmost. **Do:** Read the active tab URL. **If:** That URL equals the article you chose and Safari is still frontmost. **Do:** Press Space once to advance the article.

## Choose the article and pace

1. Import the disabled Rule. In the article URL Condition, replace the demonstration Mac automation guide URL with your article's exact URL.
2. Adjust Timed Repeat from 30 seconds to your reading pace. It is a timer, not an estimate of whether you finished reading.
3. Allow Accessibility and Automation for Safari. Timed Repeat, Get Current Tab and Type Text or Press Keys require Pro.
4. Open the chosen article in Safari and focus its body. Reader mode can help remove forms and other controls; use it only if the page supports it.
5. Enable the Rule, watch its first advance and adjust the interval if needed.
6. Switch tabs or apps to pause matching events. Disable the Rule when you finish reading.

## Scope and focus

The URL comparison is exact, including a trailing slash or query string. The sample URL is `https://www.rulr.app/posts/mac-automation/`; it does not match every Safari tab. Returning to the chosen article resumes matching timer events until you disable the Rule.

Keep focus on the article, not the address bar, a search field or a button. The Rule checks the app and tab URL, not the focused webpage element. A change of focus during an already started event can still affect where that Space press goes.

The Rule does not detect the end of an article, wait for reading progress, produce smooth scrolling, or press Space and click simultaneously. Review the first few advances on your chosen page before relying on the timer.

For a different text task, see [Letters and Alphabet Positions](/rules/letters-to-numbers-mac/).
rules.intro:
Automatically press the Spacebar on Mac to advance a long Safari article while reading hands-free. Every 30 seconds, the Rule checks Safari and the chosen article URL before sending one Space press.

Choose your article and reading interval before enabling. Switching to another app or a different article skips new matching events; the Rule never clicks the mouse.
requiredConfiguration: Choose the exact article URL in the Condition, focus the article or Reader, and adjust the reading interval; requires Pro, Accessibility and Automation for Safari
rules.title: Read an Article Hands-Free

rules.description: Review a copied web link and open it in Safari without pasting into the address bar.
rules.documentation:
## Open a copied address from a message

A colleague may send a web address as plain text rather than a clickable link. Copy that address, invoke this Rule from your current app and review it before opening a Safari tab. You do not have to switch browsers, focus the address bar, paste and submit it yourself.

**When:** Press Option + O. **Do:** Read and trim the current clipboard text. **If:** It has the form of one HTTP or HTTPS URL with no spaces. **Do:** Show the captured address for confirmation, then open it in a new Safari tab if you continue.

The input comes from the clipboard, not a fixed website stored in the Rule. The Condition filters out ordinary copied paragraphs before showing an opening prompt.

## Configure it

1. Import the disabled Rule and review Option + O.
2. Allow Accessibility and Automation for Safari. Transform Text requires Pro.
3. Enable it, copy a complete web address and invoke the Rule.
4. Check the address in the confirmation. Cancel to leave Safari unchanged, or continue to open it.
5. Copy ordinary text and invoke it again; the URL Condition should skip the opening step.

## Clipboard and URL limits

This Rule opens only the current copied link. It does not open a clipboard-history window, restore previous copies or let you select older items. If you are looking for that history behavior, this Rule does not provide it.

The expression checks the URL's basic shape, not whether a destination exists or is trustworthy. Multiple links, unencoded spaces, `mailto:` and local file paths do not pass. A malformed HTTP URL can pass the initial pattern and still fail when Safari opens it.

The clipboard is left unchanged. The opening Action uses the captured result even if another app updates the clipboard while the confirmation is visible. A successful open request is not proof the page loaded.

For copied text going into a document instead, use [Paste as Plain Text](/rules/paste-without-formatting-mac/).
rules.intro:
Open a link from your Mac clipboard in Safari after reviewing the URL. Copy a complete web address from a message or document, then run the Rule to check and open it.

The Rule snapshots and trims the current clipboard text, checks for a single HTTP or HTTPS link and asks for confirmation. It opens that same captured link without rereading the clipboard.
requiredConfiguration: Review Option + O; copy one complete HTTP or HTTPS link; requires Pro, Accessibility and Automation for Safari
rules.title: Open Clipboard Link

rules.description: Find local dictionary word candidates from 20 Quartiles tiles and open a report.
rules.documentation:
## Find words you have not noticed

Use this while reviewing a Quartiles puzzle when you want word suggestions without automatically entering words or revealing the entire official list. You supply the visible tiles; the Rule searches combinations and leaves you to try candidates in the game.

**When:** Press Option + Q. **Do:** Ask for the 20 tiles, run the embedded candidate finder and open its report in TextEdit.

The finder considers ordered combinations of one to four distinct tile positions. It matches them against the local dictionary and records each candidate's tile pieces and positions. Identical tile text in two positions can be used twice because they are two separate tiles; a single position is never reused within a candidate.

## Configure and use

1. Import the disabled Rule and review Option + Q. Allow Accessibility for its shortcut. Run Shell Script requires Pro.
2. Check that `/usr/share/dict/words` is a readable UTF-8 word list with one word per line. If absent, choose an existing word-list file you are entitled to use and update `dictionaryPath` in the embedded source. No dictionary is downloaded or bundled.
3. Enable the Rule, open the puzzle and invoke it.
4. Enter exactly 20 tile strings separated by spaces or commas. Enter each tile as one item; do not split a multi-letter tile into individual letters.
5. Review the report in TextEdit and try candidate words yourself. Check your input if the report is empty or contains unexpected suggestions.

The input accepts English letters only, with one to twelve letters per tile. Cancelling the input stops the flow. A missing dictionary, invalid input or failed report write stops the Rule rather than opening an empty result as if it succeeded.

## What the report means

The local dictionary is not Apple's vocabulary. It can include words the puzzle rejects and omit words it accepts. A match is not proof of a correct Quartiles answer. The Rule does not promise all five Quartiles, select a globally valid grouping of the full board, publish today's answers or track a puzzle date.

The report deduplicates word spellings and shows one tile grouping per word. It does not list every alternate grouping. You can reuse a tile across different suggested words, as each is an independent candidate.

Each run writes a new uniquely named report in the macOS temporary directory. Save it elsewhere from TextEdit if you want to keep it. The script returns only the report path, so the complete result is not limited by the Action's short captured-output limit.

## Dependencies and execution

The finder is JavaScript for Automation embedded in Run Shell Script and launched through the macOS `osascript` utility. It is not a native Quartiles component and does not require Python, Node or an online service. The script reads your chosen local dictionary and writes the local report; it does not control News, submit answers or use the game's reveal command.

The Action has a 120-second timeout. The word list is limited to 12 million characters. This configuration has been checked against the component contract; it has not been run or verified in the Mac App in this change.

For alphabet-position exercises, use [Letters and Alphabet Positions](/rules/letters-to-numbers-mac/).
rules.intro:
Find Quartiles word candidates on Mac by entering the puzzle's 20 tiles. The Rule checks combinations against a local word list and opens a report showing words and their tile groupings.

Ask for Input collects the tiles, an embedded script finds dictionary matches, and Open File or Folder opens the report in TextEdit. Results are candidate words, not a verified daily Apple News answer list.
requiredConfiguration: Review Option + Q; enter 20 tiles; requires Pro and a readable UTF-8 word list at /usr/share/dict/words or your configured path; results are not verified Apple answers
rules.title: Find Quartiles Word Candidates
